author: copilot
body:
`Float64(String(py_list[i]))` in the `from_pandas` float64 branch routes values through a decimal string, which is lossy for floats requiring more than ~15 significant digits (subnormals, near-max values, repeating decimals).

## Changes

- **`bison/column.mojo`** — Replace the string round-trip with a bit-exact extraction: `struct.pack("d", v)` → `struct.unpack("q", ...)` → `bitcast[DType.float64]`. The `"q"` (signed int64) unpack format is used instead of `"Q"` (unsigned) to avoid `Int` overflow on values with the sign bit set (i.e. all negative floats). Adds `from memory import bitcast`.

- **`tests/test_interop.mojo`** — Adds `test_float64_bitcast_roundtrip`, which asserts exact IEEE-754 bit preservation across `from_pandas` for five boundary cases: smallest subnormal, near-max positive, near-max negative, zero, and `1/3`.

```mojo
# before — lossy for extreme values
data.append(Float64(String(py_list[i])))

# after — bit-exact
var packed = struct_mod.unpack("q", struct_mod.pack("d", py_list[i]))
var bits = Int64(Int(py=packed[0]))
data.append(bitcast[DType.float64](bits))
```

> Note: `bitcast[DType.float64]` (the `DType`-parameterised overload from `memory`) is available in Mojo 0.26.1, even though the issue flagged `UnsafePointer.address_of` and `memory.bitcast` as blocked — those refer to the pointer-based overloads, not this scalar form.

Ref: A-459
1. barretenberg/docs had a broken resolution `"@docusaurus/mdx-loader/image-size": "1.2.1"` (added in PR #17462) that never worked. Changed to `"@docusaurus/**/image-size": "1.2.1"` which is the correct yarn v1 syntax. 

2. barretenberg/docs/yarn.lock required `yarn --ignore-scripts` to save lockfile changes. The regular `yarn` fails on netlify's postinstall script (`@netlify/dev-utils` export error on Node.js v24), which prevents the lockfile from being written. 3.  boxes/yarn.lock still has tar@6.2.1 via tiged@2.12.7 (requests ^6.1.11). 6.2.1 is the latest tar v6. tiged@3.0.0-rc.0 uses tar v7 but is not stable yet.

body:
### Checklist

#### General

- [x] I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types.
- [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://confluence.aet.cit.tum.de/spaces/AP/pages/257786006/Language+Guidelines+Client).
- [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://confluence.aet.cit.tum.de/spaces/AP/pages/256311714/PR+Guidelines).

#### Client

- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a very good performance, prevented too many (unnecessary) REST calls and made sure the UI is responsive, even with large data (e.g. using paging).
- [x] I **strictly** followed the principle of **data economy** for all client-server REST calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [client coding and design guidelines](https://confluence.aet.cit.tum.de/spaces/AP/pages/256311716/Client+Guidelines).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Jest) related to the features (with a high test coverage), while following the [test guidelines](https://confluence.aet.cit.tum.de/spaces/AP/pages/256311925/Client+Test+Guidelines).
- [x] I documented the TypeScript code using JSDoc style.

### Motivation and Context

Closes #2208

Running client tests on `main` produces numerous warnings that pollute CI logs and make it harder to identify real failures. This PR eliminates all of them.

### Description

**1. Fix "disabled attribute with a reactive form directive" warnings (6 occurrences)**
- Removed `[disabled]` from `string-input.component.html` and `checkbox.component.html` on the `@if (control())` branches where `[formControl]` is also used.
- Added a programmatic `ctrl.disable()` / `ctrl.enable()` effect in `BaseInputDirective` to sync the disabled state without triggering Angular's warning.
- `[disabled]` is kept on the `@else` (ngModel) branches where it is safe.

**2. Remove deprecated `allowSignalWrites` option**
- Removed `{ allowSignalWrites: true }` from effects in `sorting.ts`, `search-filter-sort-bar.ts`, and `slots-section.component.ts`.
- This option is deprecated since Angular 19 as signal writes in effects are now allowed by default.

**3. Add `IntersectionObserver` mock for jsdom**
- Added a no-op `MockIntersectionObserver` implementing the full `IntersectionObserver` interface in `test-setup.ts`.
- Prevents `ReferenceError` in components that use `IntersectionObserver` (e.g. progress-stepper).

**4. Add `runSilently` test utility**
- Added a global `runSilently<T>(fn: () => T): T` helper that suppresses `console.error`, `console.warn`, and `console.info` for the duration of a function.
- Applied to 6 test call sites that intentionally trigger errors (failed uploads, 409 conflicts, etc.).
- Works with both sync and async functions; console methods are always restored.

### Steps for Testing

Prerequisites:

1. Check out this branch
2. Run `npx vitest run` and verify all tests pass with no warnings about:
   - "disabled attribute with a reactive form directive"
   - `allowSignalWrites`
   - `IntersectionObserver` ReferenceError

### Review Progress

#### Code Review

- [x] Code Review 1

#### Manual Tests

- [x] Test 1 — Verify `npx vitest run` passes with zero warnings

### Screenshots

N/A — no UI changes, test infrastructure only.

body:
## Summary
- Adds 28 dedicated unit tests for file-watch-service lifecycle and cleanup behavior
- Verifies resource cleanup (FSWatcher close, debounce timer clearing, listener removal) across all teardown paths
- Closes #654

## Changes
- **Window close cleanup tests**: Verify `cleanupWatchesForWindow` closes FSWatchers, clears debounce timers, removes destroyed listeners, handles multiple watches per window, and isolates watches from other windows
- **Sender destruction cleanup tests**: Verify destroyed event triggers full resource cleanup, no events leak after destruction, pending debounce is handled gracefully, and only the affected watch is cleaned up
- **Application shutdown tests**: Verify `stopAllWatches` closes all FSWatchers, removes all destroyed listeners, clears all pending debounce timers, empties the activeWatches map, and is safe to call multiple times
- **Error resilience tests**: Verify cleanup continues when `watcher.close()` throws, and the watch is still removed from the map

- [x] Lint clean for changed files (2 pre-existing errors in unrelated files)

author: gondeknp
body:
Noticed 2 sneaky bugs regarding runRemote - (1) was that exports were not rendering properly due to a mismatch of between `uri` and the stem the frontend looks for - (memory://editor/patches) vs just `patches`, and (2) appending rather than the expected overwrite behavior, which originally manifested as a duckdb read error but actually occured because of colliding runs with different export cols. 

Now the expected behavior: 

```
  Route 1 — runRemote (static path, all replicates): one factory, opened once, stream stays open for all
  replicates. Overwrite on open is safe because nothing re-opens between replicates.
  # Run twice — second run should overwrite first
  ./gradlew shadowJar && java -jar build/libs/joshsim-fat.jar runRemote ...

  Route 2 — run with {replicate} in path: routes through buildParameterizedCsv, each replicate gets its own
  fresh file. No append involved at all.

  Route 3 — run with static path (the common case, e.g. simple.josh): one factory per replicate,
  opened/closed independently. totalReplicateCount > 1 means replicate 0 overwrites (fresh session start),
  replicates 1+ append within the same session. A second invocation resets and overwrites again.
 ```

author: binbandit
body: ## Summary Adds GitLab (`glab` CLI) support for the PR/MR creation flow, alongside the existing GitHub (`gh`) support. The hosting provider is detected automatically from the repository's `origin` remote URL — no user configuration required. Closes #535 Closes #191 ## Architecture The existing `GitHubCli` Effect service is kept as the GitHub-specific implementation (with Schema-validated JSON decoders, error normalization, etc.). This PR adds a **provider-agnostic `GitHostingCli` service** that acts as the interface consumed by `GitManager`, with a **dispatcher layer** that delegates to `GitHubCli` for GitHub repos and implements `glab` CLI calls inline for GitLab repos: ``` GitHostingCli (service contract — consumed by GitManager) │ └── GitHostingCliDispatcher (runtime layer) │ ├── detectHostingProvider(cwd) │ └── git remote get-url origin → parse hostname │ ├── github.com / *.github.com → "github" │ ├── gitlab.com / *.gitlab.com → "gitlab" │ └── unknown → "github" (backwards-compatible default) │ ├── "github" → delegates to GitHubCli service (dependency) │ └── GitHubCliLive (Schema-validated gh JSON parsing) │ └── "gitlab" → inline glab CLI calls └── glab mr list / glab mr view / glab mr create / glab repo view Layer wiring (serverLayers.ts): GitHostingCliLive ─── provides ──→ GitHubCliLive GitManagerLive ─── depends on ─→ GitHostingCliLive ``` ### Detection logic `detectHostingProvider(cwd)` runs `git remote get-url origin`, **parses the URL hostname** (supports both `https://` and `git@` formats), and matches against `gitlab.com` / `*.gitlab.com`. Results are **cached per repository path** so detection only runs once per `cwd`. Falls back to GitHub for unknown or missing remotes, preserving full backwards compatibility. ### Key design decisions - **GitHubCli is kept unchanged** — all existing GitHub-specific Schema types (`GitHubPullRequestSummary`, `GitHubRepositoryCloneUrls`), JSON decoders, and the `GitHubCli.test.ts` unit tests from main's PR #718 are preserved as-is. - **GitHostingCli is the superset interface** — includes all 7 methods: `execute`, `listOpenPullRequests`, `getPullRequest`, `getRepositoryCloneUrls`, `createPullRequest`, `getDefaultBranch`, `checkoutPullRequest`. - **`GitHubCliError` is a deprecated alias** for `GitHostingCliError` (same `_tag: "GitHostingCliError"`), so existing error-handling code continues to work. ## Changes | File | Change | |------|--------| | `apps/server/src/git/Services/GitHostingCli.ts` | **New** — Provider-agnostic service contract (`GitHostingCliShape`, `PullRequestSummary`, `RepositoryCloneUrls`, `GitHostingCli` tag) | | `apps/server/src/git/Layers/GitHostingCliDispatcher.ts` | **New** — Runtime dispatcher: detects provider, delegates to `GitHubCli` for GitHub, implements `glab` inline for GitLab | | `apps/server/src/git/Errors.ts` | Add `GitHostingCliError` class; `GitHubCliError` kept as deprecated alias | | `apps/server/src/git/Layers/GitManager.ts` | Consume `GitHostingCli` instead of `GitHubCli` (5 call sites) | | `apps/server/src/git/Layers/CodexTextGeneration.ts` | PR prompt text made provider-agnostic | | `apps/server/src/serverLayers.ts` | Wire `GitHostingCliLive` layer with `GitHubCliLive` as dependency | | `apps/server/src/git/Layers/GitManager.test.ts` | Updated to use `GitHostingCliError` / `GitHostingCli` / `PullRequestSummary` types | ### GitLab CLI commands used | Operation | Command | |-----------|---------| | List open MRs | `glab mr list --source-branch --per-page --output json` | | View MR | `glab mr view --output json` | | Create MR | `glab mr create --target-branch --source-branch --title --description <body> --yes` | | Checkout MR | `glab mr checkout <id>` | | Repo clone URLs | `glab repo view <repo> --output json` → `http_url_to_repo`, `ssh_url_to_repo` | | Default branch | `glab repo view --output json` → `default_branch` | ## Testing - `bun lint` — 0 errors - `bun typecheck` — 0 errors across all 7 packages - `bun fmt:check` — all files formatted - GitManager tests: all 29 pass (including main's new fork/worktree/PR thread tests) - GitHubCli tests: all 3 pass (Schema decoder tests from main, preserved unchanged) <!-- Macroscope's pull request summary starts here --> <!-- Macroscope will only edit the content between these invisible markers, and the markers themselves will not be visible in the GitHub rendered markdown. --> <!-- If you delete either of the start / end markers from your PR's description, Macroscope will append its summary at the bottom of the description. --> > [!NOTE] > ### Add GitLab `glab` CLI support for merge request operations > - Introduces a new `GitHostingCli` abstraction and `GitHostingCliDispatcher` that routes all PR/MR operations (`listPullRequests`, `createPullRequest`, `checkoutPullRequest`, etc.) to either `gh` or `glab` based on the repository's remote origin hostname. > - Replaces all direct `GitHubCli` references in `GitManager` with the new `GitHostingCli` interface, making hosting-provider detection transparent to callers. > - Adds `hostingPlatform` ('github'|'gitlab') and `hostingCliAuthenticated` (boolean|null) fields to `GitStatusResult`, surfaced from the dispatcher's cached auth checks. > - Updates the web UI (`GitActionsControl`, `Sidebar`, `pullRequestReference`) to use platform-aware PR/MR labels, icons, and disabled states — including downgrading PR creation to push-only when the hosting CLI is unauthenticated. > - Risk: all consumers of `GitStatusResult` must now handle the two new required fields; the `GitHostingCliError` tag replaces `GitHubCliError` (backward-compat aliases provided). > > <!-- Macroscope's review summary starts here --> > > <sup><a href="https://app.macroscope.com">Macroscope</a> summarized 9095394.</sup> > <!-- Macroscope's review summary ends here --> > > <!-- macroscope-ui-refresh --> <!-- Macroscope's pull request summary ends here -->

author: macwilling
body:
## Problem

After merging #83, clicking the invite email link left clients stuck on the "Signing you in…" page indefinitely.

`@supabase/ssr` forces `flowType: 'pkce'` on the browser client, so it only scans for `?code=` in query params and silently ignores `#access_token=` hash tokens. Admin-generated magic links use the OTP/implicit flow and redirect with hash tokens, so `onAuthStateChange` never fired `SIGNED_IN` — the component waited forever.

## Fix

Replace the `onAuthStateChange` listener with direct hash parsing:
1. Extract `access_token` + `refresh_token` from `window.location.hash`
2. Call `supabase.auth.setSession()` — bypasses the flow-type restriction and stores tokens in the `@supabase/ssr` cookie adapter
3. Call `finalizePortalSessionAction` once cookies are set, then redirect
4. Clear the hash from the URL to prevent re-triggering on back-navigation

## Test plan

- [ ] Admin sends portal invite → client clicks email link → lands on portal dashboard (not stuck)
- [ ] Clicking a used/expired link → redirected to portal login with error
- [ ] Direct navigation to `/portal/[slug]/auth-callback` without tokens → redirected to login
- [ ] Already-signed-in user hits the page → redirected straight to portal

author: tyler-reitz
body:
## PR Description

  This PR implements an event-driven order processing architecture using local AWS emulation.

  - order-api (FastAPI) writes new orders to Postgres as PENDING and publishes OrderCreated to SNS (orders-topic).
  - SNS fan-outs to SQS queues consumed by workers:
      - inventory-worker: handles OrderCreated, reserves stock, emits OrderAccepted/OrderRejected
      - order-status-worker: updates order status in Postgres (ACCEPTED/REJECTED)
      - notification-worker: writes mock notifications for accepted/rejected events
      - analytics-worker: maintains per-event-type counters
  - Reliability/idempotency: workers record processed event IDs in processed_events to avoid duplicate processing.
  - Infra is fully local via Docker Compose: Postgres + LocalStack (SNS/SQS/EventBridge) + API + workers.

  ## How to Run

  make up
  make bootstrap
  make smoke   # recommended end-to-end check

  Useful checks:

  curl -sS http://localhost:8000/health
  docker compose logs --tail=100 inventory-worker order-status-worker notification-worker analytics-worker

## PR description
`eth_simulateV1` was returning `-32602 Invalid params` when both `input`                                                                                                                      
  and `data` fields were provided with different values, while all other EL                                                                                                                     
  clients (Geth, Nethermind, Reth, Erigon) silently accept this and use                                                                                                                         
  `input`.

  This is fixed with a targeted deserializer (`SimulateCallParameterDeserializer`)

  defined in `GenericTransaction`.

  retain the existing strict validation that errors when `input` and `data`
  conflict, matching Geth's behaviour for those methods.

body: ## Problem Multiple Sentry issues are actively firing due to ClickHouse queries exceeding the 15s `max_execution_time`: | Issue | Events | Page | Error | |-------|--------|------|-------| | CODE-REVIEW-TRENDS-3 | 281 | `/status` | Timeout exceeded: 15015ms | | CODE-REVIEW-TRENDS-15 | 593 | `/orgs/[owner]` | Slow DB Query | | CODE-REVIEW-TRENDS-H | 45 | `/status` | Server Components render error | | CODE-REVIEW-TRENDS-J | 167 | `/status` | Hydration Error | | WORKER-29/28/2M/2K | ~32 | warmup | Warmup failed: HTTP 500 | **Root cause:** Several queries still scan raw `pr_bot_events` (7M+ rows) despite pre-aggregated materialized views being available (`pr_bot_event_counts`, `repo_pr_summary`, `org_pr_summary`). ## Fix Replace raw table scans with MV reads. The 15s timeout stays — queries must be fast, not given more time. ### Query optimizations | Function | Before | After | |----------|--------|-------| | `getOrgSummary` | `countDistinct` on raw `pr_bot_events` + JOIN repos | `uniqExactMerge` on `pr_bot_event_counts` MV (471K rows) | | `getOrgRepos` | `countDistinct(pr_number)` on raw `pr_bot_events` | `uniqExactMerge` on `repo_pr_summary` MV | | `getOrgProducts` | Full scan of `pr_bot_events` + `pr_bot_reactions` with NOT EXISTS | `pr_bot_event_counts` + `reaction_only_repo_counts` MVs | | `getDataCollectionStats` (×3 unreachable counts) | `count(DISTINCT) FROM pr_bot_events JOIN repos` | `repo_pr_summary` + `pr_bot_event_counts` MVs | ### Other improvements - **CTE `owner_repos`** shared across subqueries (was repeated 3-4× per query) - **IN-subquery instead of JOIN repos** for pr_comments — uses primary key index on `repo_name` - **`getOrgSummary` 5-min cache** — avoids duplicate expensive queries (`generateMetadata` + render) - **Status page query split** — 3 → 5 parallel queries (old "Query B" with 10 subqueries split into repos/PRs, comments, reactions) ---

author: latentcollapse
body:
## Summary

Passive security audit of the DreamServer codebase performed with gitleaks 8.x, bandit 1.9.4, semgrep (auto config), and shellcheck. No live infrastructure was accessed — Apache 2.0 license permits full static analysis.

**Findings:**

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 1 |
| High | 3 |
| Medium | 5 |
| Low | 2 |

### Critical — C1: Likely real LiveKit credentials committed to public repo

`resources/frameworks/voice-agent/core/hvac-token-server.py:19-20` contains format-valid LiveKit credentials (15-char API key, 43-char secret). The file header reads `Deploy to: /home/michael/hvac-token-server.py`. These match the format of real LiveKit credentials exactly and appear to be production values, not placeholders.

**Recommended action:** Rotate at console.livekit.io immediately, then purge from git history.

### High findings

- **H1:** SearXNG ships a static `secret_key` in `settings.yml` — session forgery possible on all default installs
- **H2:** `eval "$env_out"` in the installer ingests GPU metadata from nvidia-smi — command injection surface if the pipeline is influenced
- **H3:** OpenClaw `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth: true` still present (separate from PR #67 which fixed the binding issue)

### Medium / Low

SQL injection pattern in token-spy, containers running as root, nginx H2C smuggling conditions, insecure `ws://` WebSocket fallback, `local` keyword outside function scope (shellcheck SC2168), missing SRI on CDN scripts, missing security headers on dreamserver.ai.

## Full report

See `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` in this PR for complete findings, file locations, and remediation guidance for each item.

## Notes

- No live infrastructure was accessed or tested
- The C1 credential finding is a responsible disclosure — recommend rotating before merging/publicizing
- PRs #67–#70 from this contributor address several of the High findings directly

author: herbhall
body:
## Summary

- Adds `AddWorkers(n int) error` and `RemoveWorkers(n int) int` to scale the pool at runtime without restarting
- Adds `Workers() int` to query current target worker count
- Workers exit gracefully after completing their current task via a buffered `workerQuit` channel
- `RemoveWorkers` preserves minimum one worker to maintain liveness
- Fixes latent deadlock in `processTask`: `onComplete` callback was read under `p.mu`, which deadlocked when `Submit` held `p.mu` during a blocking channel send. Fixed by storing `onComplete` in `sync/atomic.Pointer`, removing the lock from the read path entirely

## Test plan

- [x] `TestWorkers` — initial count returned correctly
- [x] `TestAddWorkers` — worker count increases; new workers process tasks
- [x] `TestAddWorkers_Noop` — n ≤ 0 is a no-op
- [x] `TestAddWorkers_AfterShutdown` — returns `ErrPoolShutdown`
- [x] `TestAddWorkers_NewWorkersProcessTasks` — scaled workers drain queued tasks via Shutdown
- [x] `TestRemoveWorkers_ReducesCount` — count decreases by requested amount
- [x] `TestRemoveWorkers_MinimumOne` — single-worker pool: removes 0, count stays 1
- [x] `TestRemoveWorkers_Noop` — n ≤ 0 returns 0, count unchanged
- [x] `TestRemoveWorkers_ClampsToMinimum` — excess removes clamped to keep 1 worker
- [x] `TestPool_ConcurrentSubmitAndShutdown` — deadlock now fixed, races cleanly

Added `get`, `hincrby`, `hgetall`, `pfadd`, `pfcount`, `expire` to `StandardRedisPipelineAdapter` - Added `hincrby`, `hgetall`, `pfadd`, `pfcount` to `StandardRedisAdapter` - Updated 22 files to import `Redis` from the adapter instead of `@upstash/redis` - Only 2 files now import from `@upstash/redis`: the adapter itself, and `middleware.ts` (Vercel Edge Runtime — cannot use ioredis) **Backend — Analytics Tracking (optimized)** - New `api/_utils/_analytics.ts` module with fire-and-forget per-request tracking - **Write path**: 5–8 Redis commands per request in 1 pipeline (HINCRBY + PFADD) - **EXPIRE** runs once per calendar day per process (not every request) — saves 4–5 redundant commands per request - **Read path**: single pipeline for detail view (5 commands/day × N days in 1 round-trip) - author: copilot
body:
`lsmod` shows `fuse ... 1` — `gvfsd-fuse` is running with an active FUSE mount (`~/.gvfs` or `/run/user/<uid>/gvfs`). Because `gvfsd` waits for `gvfsd-fuse` to exit before it can terminate, every previous approach of killing `gvfsd` left it alive, allowing it to restart `gvfsd-mtp`, which reclaimed the camera's PTP session before the next capture attempt. Additionally, gvfs was only killed *reactively* after failure — the window between `is_camera_connected()` and `--capture-image-and-download` was enough for it to reclaim the session.

## `camera.py`

- **`_kill_gvfs_monitor()`**: Call `fusermount -uz` on both common gvfs mount points *before* any `pkill`; add `pkill -f gvfsd-fuse` to the sequence (must precede `pkill gvfsd`); log non-zero `fusermount` exits at `DEBUG`; expand docstring to document the FUSE dependency chain
- **`capture_image()`**: Add a **proactive** `_kill_gvfs_monitor()` call before the retry loop — previously only called reactively between failed attempts, leaving the first attempt always racing against a live gvfs session

```python
# Before: only killed gvfs AFTER a PTP error
for attempt in range(_PTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
    result = _run(["--capture-image-and-download", ...], cwd=tmpdir)
    if ptp_error:
        _kill_gvfs_monitor()   # reactive — too late for attempt 0
        continue

# After: kill proactively, then also between retries
_kill_gvfs_monitor()           # proactive — camera is free before attempt 0
for attempt in range(_PTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
    result = _run(["--capture-image-and-download", ...], cwd=tmpdir)
    if ptp_error:
        _kill_gvfs_monitor()   # reactive — still present for subsequent retries
        continue
```

## `install.sh`

- Add `fusermount -uz` before the `pkill` loop in the gvfs shutdown section
- Add two `ExecStartPre` fusermount lines in the systemd service file using `%U`/`%h` specifiers, ordered before `pkill gvfsd-fuse`

## Tests

- 4 new tests: `gvfsd-fuse` is killed, `fusermount -uz` is called, unmount precedes kill, gvfs is killed before the first capture attempt
- 4 updated retry-count tests: expected kill counts incremented by 1 to reflect the new proactive kill

# Puppeteerを使ったスクレイピング機能を追加

## Summary

管理者画面にPuppeteer（Node.js）を使用したWebスクレイピング機能を追加します。

**構成:**
- `src/node_scripts/scraper.js` — Puppeteerでヘッドレスブラウザを起動し、指定URLからページ情報（タイトル、メタデータ、見出し、リンク、画像）やスクリーンショットをJSON形式で返すNode.jsスクリプト
- `src/app/Services/PuppeteerService.php` — Laravel側からNode.jsスクリプトを`exec()`で呼び出すサービスクラス
- `src/app/Http/Controllers/Admin/ScrapingController.php` — 入力画面表示と実行のコントローラ
- `src/resources/views/admin/scraping/` — 入力フォーム（index）と結果表示（result）のBladeビュー
- `src/routes/admin.php` — `auth:admin`ミドルウェア内にスクレイピング用ルート追加
- `docker/php-apache/Dockerfile` — Node.js 20.x、Chromium、日本語フォントのインストール追加
- ダッシュボードとナビゲーションにスクレイピングへのリンクを追加

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Dockerfileの`npm install`が不足**: Dockerfileで`node_scripts/`内の`npm install`が実行されていません。Puppeteerパッケージが利用できるよう、Dockerfileまたはentrypointに`cd /var/www/html/node_scripts && npm install`を追加するか、手動で実行する手順をREADMEに記載する必要があります
- [ ] **Chromiumバイナリパスの確認**: `ENV PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium`が実際のDockerイメージ内のパスと一致するか確認してください（Debianバージョンによっては`/usr/bin/chromium-browser`の場合があります）
- [ ] **`exec()` + `2>&1`の安全性**: PuppeteerService内で`exec($command . ' 2>&1')`としているため、Node.jsがstderrに警告を出力した場合、JSON出力と混ざってパースが失敗する可能性があります
- [ ] **結果ビューのXSS**: スクレイピングで取得した`href`値をそのまま`<a href="">`に埋め込んでいます。Bladeの`{{ }}`でエスケープされますが、`javascript:`スキーム等のリンクが表示される可能性を確認してください
- [ ] **エンドツーエンドテスト**: Docker環境で実際にスクレイピングを実行し、Puppeteerが正しく動作するか検証してください（Node.jsパッケージインストール後）

### Test Plan
1. Dockerイメージをリビルド: `docker-compose build`
2. コンテナ内で`cd /var/www/html/node_scripts && npm install`を実行してPuppeteerをインストール
3. 管理者でログインし、ダッシュボードからスクレイピングリンクをクリック
4. 任意のURLとCSSセレクタ（例: `h1`）を入力してスクレイピング実行
5. 結果画面でタイトル、スクリーンショット、取得要素一覧が正しく表示されることを確認
6. 無効なURLやタイムアウトするURLでエラーハンドリングが正常に動作するか確認

### Notes
- システムnoteによりSelenium/ChromeDriverが推奨されましたが、ユーザーがPuppeteerを明示的に要求したためPuppeteerで実装しました
- ヘッドレスモードで動作するため、CAPTCHAや認証が必要なページには対応していません
- スクリーンショットはBase64エンコードでDBに保存せず、その場で表示するのみです（サイズに注意）

author: cto-new[bot]
body:
## What changed
- Added first-class `USE_LOCAL_GRAPHRAG` configuration and relaxed validation so local mode only requires LLM settings.
- Refactored graph building into a provider-aware facade that supports both existing Zep-backed graphs and a new durable local graph path.
- Implemented local graph persistence under backend uploads and added local graph IDs so the existing frontend contract continues to work.
- Added local LLM-based entity/relation extraction and graph assembly so step 02 can produce non-empty graph data without Zep.
- Introduced a provider-aware entity reader used by simulation APIs and simulation preparation so downstream entity loading works with local graphs too.
- Updated `.env.example` to document local mode.

## Why
The branch previously advertised local GraphRAG via env configuration, but the backend was still hard-wired to Zep Cloud for graph creation, graph retrieval, and entity reads. In local mode that caused step 02 graph construction to fail or produce no usable graph data. These changes make local mode an actual supported execution path while preserving the existing API surface for the frontend.

## Notable implementation details
- `GraphBuilderService` is now a facade over `ZepGraphBuilder` and `LocalGraphBuilder`.
- Local graphs are saved as JSON artifacts and exposed through the same `/api/graph/data/{graph_id}` endpoint shape expected by the frontend.
- Local extraction merges entities by normalized `(type, name)` and resolves relations against merged node identities.
- Simulation entity loading now routes through `GraphEntityReader`, which selects local or Zep readers based on config.
- Zep-only reporting/search paths were left untouched, but local graph IDs and provider-aware entity access now support ontology -> graph build -> simulation prep flow.

## Verification steps
1. Set `.env` with `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL_NAME`, and `USE_LOCAL_GRAPHRAG=true`, with no `ZEP_API_KEY`.
2. Start the backend and confirm it no longer fails config validation for missing Zep credentials.
3. Upload a test document and run step 01 ontology generation.
4. Run step 02 graph build and verify the async task completes successfully.
5. Call `GET /api/graph/data/{graph_id}` and confirm non-empty `nodes` and graph JSON persisted locally.
6. Create/prepare a simulation and confirm entity loading works against the local graph.

## Root cause summary
The root cause was that local GraphRAG had not actually been implemented. The frontend sequence was already correct, but backend graph build/read/delete and simulation entity reads were all Zep-only. Removing the Zep key check alone would not have fixed the issue; a real local build-and-persist path was required.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent insecure default JWT signing by removing the fallback secret and requiring an explicit `JWT_SECRET` when authentication is enabled.
- Fail fast on server start / requests if authentication is configured without a proper signing key to avoid unpredictable or trivially-guessable tokens.

### Description
- Removed the built-in fallback `aimodelapi-default-secret` and changed `nuxt.config.ts` to load `jwtSecret` from `process.env.JWT_SECRET` with an empty default (`''`).
- Added a guard in the login route (`server/api/auth/login.post.ts`) that throws a 500 error when `AUTH_KEY` is set but `JWT_SECRET` is missing, and use `config.jwtSecret` directly when signing tokens.
- Added a guard in the auth middleware (`server/middleware/auth.ts`) that throws a 500 error if `AUTH_KEY` is enabled but `JWT_SECRET` is not configured, and verify tokens with `config.jwtSecret` only.
- Updated `.env.example` and `README.md` to document that `JWT_SECRET` is mandatory when `AUTH_KEY` is set and to recommend a strong random secret.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` and the production build completed successfully (Nuxt build artifacts generated); Tailwind sourcemap warnings were emitted but did not block the build.
- No additional automated tests were present or modified as part of this change.

author: aaronontheweb
body:
## Summary

- `MemoryCurationWorkerService.RunAsync` now wraps the entire worker loop in an outer `try/catch (OperationCanceledException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested)` that logs at Debug and returns cleanly — so `StopAsync` can `await _worker` without the task surfacing as an error
- Inner per-checkpoint `catch` block re-throws `OperationCanceledException` immediately, preventing a shutdown-triggered cancellation from being misclassified as a curation failure and attempting a retry against an already-cancelled token

## Root cause

`StopAsync` was calling `_cts.Cancel()` then `await _worker`. Any in-flight `Task.Delay` or store awaitable would throw `TaskCanceledException` (a subclass of `OperationCanceledException`), which propagated through `_worker` as a fault and surfaced as a crash log at daemon stop time.

## Test plan

- [ ] Start daemon, issue stop — no `TaskCanceledException` in logs
- [ ] Start daemon with a pending memory checkpoint, issue stop mid-curation — worker exits cleanly without retry attempt

## Summary
Implement `CPartMng::pppEditAllReleaseResource()` from stub to a first-pass decompilation matching the original cleanup flow.

Changes include:
- release/reset `m_materialSet` and `m_textureSet`
- free the three per-slot resource pointer lanes across 0x80 entries
- free editor receive buffer (`m_recvBuff`)
- destroy/free map-mesh entries and their container array
- free stream entries (including nested buffers) and their container array
- final cleanup of trailing USB edit buffer pointer

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/partMng`
- Function: `pppEditAllReleaseResource__8CPartMngFv`

## Progress evidence
`objdiff` before/after:
- `pppEditAllReleaseResource__8CPartMngFv`: **0.6369427% -> 83.48408%**
- `main/partMng` `.text` match: **33.06567% -> 34.659275%**

Build status:
- `ninja` completed successfully after the change.

## Plausibility rationale
This follows the expected original engine-style resource teardown sequence: release reference-counted sets, walk fixed-size slot arrays by stride, free nested allocations in stream entries, destroy map meshes before freeing containers, and null pointers immediately after deallocation.

## Technical details
- Used the decomp’s observed field offsets/loop bounds (`0x80` slot loops, `0x88` map-mesh loop) and do/while control flow patterns to align with generated PPC code.
- Preserved allocator pairing (`__dl__FPv` vs `__dla__FPv`) based on observed allocation usage.
- Kept implementation in `src/partMng.cpp` without introducing extern hacks or symbol-name coercion.

body:
## Summary
Added complete technical documentation for an automated volleyball robot system designed for the Robocon 2026 volleyball competition. This document provides a full end-to-end solution covering camera calibration, ball detection, 3D tracking, trajectory prediction, and robot control.

## Key Changes

### Documentation Structure
- **Phase 0**: Camera intrinsic calibration procedure using checkerboard pattern
- **Phase 1**: Automated HSV color space calibration node with real-time adjustment
- **Phase 2**: Real-time ball detection using HSV + circularity verification
- **Phase 3**: 3D position estimation from monocular vision with known ball diameter
- **Phase 4**: Kalman Filter tracking with gravity physics model
- **Phase 5**: Parabolic trajectory fitting and landing point prediction
- **Phase 6**: Omnidirectional chassis movement control with P-controller
- **Phase 7**: Hit timing judgment and trigger logic

### Implementation Details

**Core Nodes Documented:**
- `volleyball_hsv_calibrator.py` - Automated HSV threshold calibration (30-frame sampling with σ-based bounds)
- `ball_detector.py` - HSV-based detection with morphological filtering and circularity validation
- `ball_3d_estimator.py` - Monocular depth estimation using focal length and known ball diameter
- `ball_kalman_tracker.py` - 6-state Kalman filter (position + velocity) with gravity compensation
- `landing_predictor.py` - RANSAC-based parabolic fitting for landing point prediction
- `chassis_controller.py` - P-control based velocity command generation
- Hit timing logic with response delay compensation

**Key Technical Features:**
- Single-camera depth formula: `depth = (fx × BALL_D/2) / pixel_radius`
- Kalman state transition includes gravity: `Vz(k+1) = Vz(k) - g·dt`
- RANSAC polynomial fitting for robust trajectory estimation
- ROS 2 Humble with py_trees behavior tree framework
- Comprehensive parameter tuning guide with real-world calibration procedures

### Tuning & Calibration
- Detailed parameter adjustment tables for each phase
- Problem diagnosis guide mapping symptoms to root causes
- Recommended calibration sequence and typical parameter values
- ROS 2 topic interface documentation (input/output/intermediate)

### Testing & Validation
- Includes debug visualization publishers for each processing stage
- Suggests high-speed camera validation for hit timing accuracy
- Provides fallback HSV values and graceful degradation strategies

author: martinamps
body:
Adds a **stateless Streamable HTTP MCP server** at `/mcp` — no extra dependencies, pure JSON-RPC 2.0 over Bun's existing HTTP server.

## Why

AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, etc.) can now query live Starlink tracker data via the standard [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). Users can ask their assistant "does UA544 tomorrow have Starlink?" and get a live answer.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `check_flight(flight_number, date)` | Check if a specific flight has Starlink |
| `get_fleet_stats()` | Installation progress across mainline/express fleets |
| `list_starlink_aircraft(fleet?, limit?)` | Enumerate equipped planes |
| `search_starlink_flights(origin?, destination?, limit?)` | Find Starlink flights by route |

## Implementation

- **Zero dependencies** — no MCP SDK needed, ~430 LOC in one file
- **Stateless** — no sessions, no SSE push, each request independent
- **Free to run** — same process, same DB handle as the existing server
- **Spec-compliant** with MCP `2025-06-18` / `2025-03-26`:
  - `initialize` / `tools/list` / `tools/call` / `ping`
  - `notifications/initialized` → `202 Accepted`
  - `GET` / `DELETE` → `405 Method Not Allowed` (stateless, no push, no sessions)
  - Proper JSON-RPC error codes (`-32700` parse, `-32601` method not found, `-32602` invalid params, `-32603` internal)
  - Tool-level errors use `result.isError` (business logic errors are still HTTP 200)

## Connect

From any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, MCP Inspector):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ua-starlink": {
      "url": "https://unitedstarlinktracker.com/mcp",
      "transport": "http"
    }
  }
}
```

## Testing

14 test cases verified locally against the live handler:

```
✓ initialize → protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo, instructions
✓ notifications/initialized → HTTP 202
✓ tools/list → 4 tools with JSON Schema
✓ ping → {}
✓ get_fleet_stats → formatted stats text
✓ list_starlink_aircraft (fleet=express, limit=3) → filtered & limited
✓ check_flight (no match) → helpful message
✓ check_flight (bad date) → isError: true
✓ search_starlink_flights (origin=ORD) → works
✓ search_starlink_flights (no args) → isError: true
✓ Unknown method → JSON-RPC error -32601
✓ Unknown tool → JSON-RPC error -32602
✓ Bad JSON → JSON-RPC error -32700, HTTP 400
✓ Wrong Content-Type → HTTP 415
✓ GET /mcp → HTTP 405
```

Also added to `/llms.txt` so AI crawlers discover it.

- Extended trigger engine to enforce role allowlists and cooldowns, to increment stats only when allowed, and to support milestone templates with new placeholders (`{milestone}`, `{next_milestone}`, `{remaining_to_next_milestone}`, `{count_user_prev}`); template resolution now prefers per-user templates, then milestone template, then global templates, then fallback.
- Enhanced the command surface in `register_triggers` for `frasi` with `add`, `edit`, `list`, `stats`, and milestone commands (`milestone_set`, `milestone_remove`, `milestone_list`), input parsing helpers for roles and improved display formatting/humanized timestamps.
- Updated tests in `tests/test_trigger_phrases_global.py` and added multiple unit tests covering DB serialization, cooldown behavior, role allow/block logic, edit/reset semantics, milestone triggering and priority, and the new admin commands.

### Testing
- Ran the updated unit tests in `tests/test_trigger_phrases_global.py` which exercise DB migrations, add/edit/list commands, cooldown semantics, role allowlist behavior, milestone creation/removal/listing, and stats reporting; all tests passed locally.

# Overview

Add `useSet` hook that manages a Set as state, mirroring the `useMap` pattern.

- `add` / `remove` for adding and removing values
- `toggle` adds the value if absent, removes it if present

- `reset` restores the set to its initial state
- Accepts `Set<T>` or `T[]` as initial state

body:
### Motivation
- Guarantee that the auth-service always has a default administrator account available after application startup for initial access and testing.
- Avoid creating duplicate accounts on repeated startups by making the initializer idempotent.

### Description
- Updated `Services/auth-service/src/main/java/com/debtmanager/authservice/config/DataInitializer.java` to provide a `CommandLineRunner` bean (`initAdminUser`) that runs at startup.
- The initializer checks `userRepository.findByEmail("admin@debtmanager.com")` and only creates the user when the lookup is empty, preventing duplicates.
- The created user uses `PasswordEncoder` to store a BCrypt-encoded password (`Admin123*`), is assigned role `ADMIN`, and is enabled.
- Added a logger and constants for the default email, password, and role, and included startup logs to indicate whether the admin was created or already existed.

### Testing
- Attempted to run unit tests with `cd Services/auth-service && mvn test -q`, but the build failed due to external dependency resolution (Maven Central returned HTTP 403 for the Spring Boot parent POM), so tests could not complete.
- No other automated tests were executed in this environment due to the dependency resolution error.

| `complexity:local` (non-critical) | Tier 1, allow |
| `complexity:cloud` + `priority:normal/high` | Tier 2, allow |
| `complexity:ambiguous` or `priority:critical` | Tier 3, skip + post comment |
| `pc-failure-N >= MaxFailures` | Skip (too many retries) |
| `depends_on` has open issues | Skip (dependency unresolved) |

author: notdp
body:
## Problem

The install flow was surfacing and treating two checks as install-time permission issues even though they are not required to complete installation:

- `karabinerInputMonitoring`
- `dictation`

That made the installer noisier than necessary and could incorrectly suggest the install was blocked when users could still finish setup and use Typeless normally.

There was also a bad deep link for the Accessibility panel, so when we *do* ask the user to fix real install-time permissions, the System Settings page could open to the wrong place.

## What this PR changes

- stop surfacing `karabinerInputMonitoring` and `dictation` in install/update permission results
- keep install-time permission gating focused on the current session permissions that actually matter for finishing setup
- centralize install-specific permission filtering in `cli/lib/install-permissions.mjs`
- fix the Accessibility System Settings deep link used by the installer flow
- add CLI tests for filtered permission output and install gating behavior

## Design

This PR separates:

- the full raw permission inspection used by diagnostics, and
- the narrower permission subset that should affect the install UX

The install command should only block or warn on permissions that are immediately relevant to completing installation. `dictation` and Karabiner Input Monitoring can still matter later in runtime, but they should not be presented as install blockers or install reminders.

## Testing

- `scripts/validate.sh`

- `apps/dashboard/src/features/pages/organization-members-settings-page-view.stories.tsx`: adds a stateful interaction story that exercises load retry, capability retry, invite dialog open/close, role dialog open/save, and invitation resend feedback through visible UI state changes.

author: hyochan
body:
## Summary

- Remove `DispatchSemaphore` blocking pattern in iOS `fetchProducts()` that caused thread starvation deadlocks
- Replace with async `Task` + signal emission pattern (matching `requestPurchase` and other iOS methods)
- Update GDScript wrapper to `await products_fetched` signal on iOS

## Root Cause

The iOS `fetchProducts()` used a `DispatchSemaphore` to bridge async StoreKit 2 calls to synchronous GDExtension returns. This blocked Godot's main thread, preventing the async `Task` from executing, causing a deadlock that always resulted in a 30-second timeout.

## Changes

### iOS (`ios-gdextension/`)
- Remove `DispatchSemaphore` and 30-second timeout logic
- Return `{"status": "pending"}` immediately (like `requestPurchase`)
- Emit results via `products_fetched` signal asynchronously

### GDScript (`addons/godot-iap/`)
- iOS path: call native `fetchProducts()` then `await products_fetched` signal
- Android path: unchanged (synchronous return)

## Test plan

- [ ] iOS: `fetch_products()` returns products without timeout
- [ ] Android: `fetch_products()` continues to work as before
- [ ] Example project runs in Godot editor

Closes #15

author: chielri
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the template matching algorithm to handle edge cases with uniform images, improves configuration management to use Pydantic v2 patterns, adds input validation for search parameters, and fixes several bugs in image dimension tracking and error handling.

## Key Changes

### Backend - Template Matching & Search
- **Zero-variance guard**: Added checks to skip template matching when query images have near-zero variance, preventing false positives from `TM_CCOEFF_NORMED` returning 1.0 everywhere on uniform templates
- **NaN handling**: Guard against NaN values in match results that can appear when page regions have zero variance, replacing them with 0.0 so they never pass confidence thresholds
- **Scale range fix**: Ensure 1.0 (original size) is always included in multi-scale matching to avoid missing exact matches
- **Input validation**: Added `@model_validator` to `SearchParams` to ensure `scale_min < scale_max`, and validate HTTP request method parameter against allowed values
- **File upload security**: Use UUID-based filenames instead of user-provided names to prevent path traversal and collisions
- **Response typing**: Added explicit `StatusResponse` model for `/status/{job_id}` endpoint and proper type hints throughout

### Backend - Configuration
- **Pydantic v2 migration**: Updated `Settings` class to use `SettingsConfigDict` instead of nested `Config` class
- **CORS handling**: Refactored `cors_origins` to store as string and added `cors_origin_list` property for parsing, improving flexibility
- **Field defaults**: Simplified field definitions by using Pydantic defaults instead of manual `os.getenv()` calls

### Frontend - Image Dimension Tracking
- **Dimension updates**: Refactored dimension tracking to use `ResizeObserver` in addition to load events, ensuring dimensions update when the image element is resized
- **Callback optimization**: Extracted dimension update logic into a `useCallback` to prevent unnecessary re-renders and event listener churn
- **Separate concerns**: Split dimension tracking into two effects: one for image loading and one for resize observation

### Frontend - Error Handling & Cleanup
- **Better error messages**: Enhanced error handling in `useSearch` hook to extract and display backend error details from Axios responses
- **Removed unused utilities**: Deleted `getFilePreviewUrl` and `revokePreviewUrl` helpers that were not being used

### Tests
- **Pattern improvements**: Updated test images to use high-contrast patterns instead of uniform colors, ensuring templates have sufficient variance for matching algorithms
- **Test assertions**: Added explicit assertions for expected behavior (e.g., `total_matches == 0` for no-match cases)

## Notable Implementation Details
- The zero-variance guard uses `query_gray.std() < 1.0` threshold to catch near-uniform templates before matching
- Multi-scale matching now explicitly appends 1.0 to the scales array if it's within the range but not already included due to linspace discretization
- The `cors_origin_list` property handles both string and list inputs for backward compatibility
- File uploads now use `uuid.uuid4().hex` for unique naming while preserving original file extensions

author: rohan5986
body:
**Related Issue:** Contributes to #43

### Context & Objective
As discussed, this PR serves as an initial prototype for the backend inference and tracing pipeline required to integrate ESMFold into VizFold. It successfully handles the heavy ML infrastructure tasks—specifically running the forward pass and extracting the required hidden states, attention maps, and predicted structures into a standardized archive format.

### Key Changes & Implementations
* **ESMFold Inference (`extract_esmfold.py`):**  Implemented model loading using the Hugging Face `transformers` library (`EsmForProteinFolding`).
  * Configured explicit cache redirection and `safetensors` enforcement to bypass HPC cluster disk quota limitations and recent PyTorch `torch.load` security blocks.
* **Attention Map Interception:**  Because the top-level ESMFold wrapper drops attention matrices, I engineered custom PyTorch forward hooks attached to the self-attention modules of all 36 Transformer layers within the ESM-2 stem to manually intercept and extract the raw attention tensors.
* **VizFold Schema Formatting (`format_vizfold.py`):**  Wrote a formatter to clean the raw PyTorch tensors and convert them to NumPy arrays.
  * Sliced out the implicit `<cls>` and `<eos>` padding tokens from the stem's attention maps to ensure sequence length alignment.
  * Isolated the final 3D structural output from the model's 8-step iterative refinement tensor.
  * Packaged the clean tensors (sequence, single representations, attention, positions) into a `.pkl` archive.

author: copilot
body:
All E2E tests were failing due to two independent issues: corrupt baseline PNG snapshots and a race condition in mobile navigation tests.

### Corrupt PNG snapshots (45 of 78 files)

Chunk-level PNG validation revealed widespread corruption — CRC mismatches in IDAT chunks, trailing bytes after IEND, truncated chunks. The `file` command masks this since it only checks magic bytes, but Playwright's parser is strict. Root cause is likely the CI screenshot merge workflow producing partial overwrites when new screenshots are shorter than old ones.

Deleted all 45 corrupt files. CI runs with `--update-snapshots` and will regenerate them.

### Mobile navigation test timing

`mobile-navigation.spec.ts` interacted with the dropdown immediately after `page.goto()` without waiting for hydration. React re-rendering during hydration disrupts the daisyUI CSS `:focus-within` dropdown state.

Added page content waits before dropdown interaction, matching the pattern already used in passing tests:

```typescript
// Before interacting with dropdown, wait for page hydration
await expect(page.locator("h1").filter({ hasText: "Notes" })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 })
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open user menu" }).click()
```

body:
### Motivation

- The monitor needs to account for the global `repeated_state_publish_interval` setting when deciding sensor staleness and whether monitoring should run at all.
- When unchanged states are not republished (`repeated_state_publish_interval < 0`) the monitor cannot infer staleness and should avoid scheduling or subscribing.
- Tests must verify the new behavior across positive, zero and negative `repeated_state_publish_interval` values.

### Description

- Added `active_config` usage and logic to `MonitorService.schedule` to return an empty task list and log when `repeated_state_publish_interval < 0` so monitoring is disabled.
- Updated `MonitorService.subscribe` to skip registering MQTT subscriptions and log when `repeated_state_publish_interval < 0`.
- Modified `MonitoredSensor.is_overdue` to consult `active_config.repeated_state_publish_interval`, returning `False` when negative, using the larger of `scan_interval` and `repeated_state_publish_interval` when the latter is positive, and falling back to `scan_interval` when zero.

author: thomas-vilte
body:
## Description
Implementé la lógica para procesar y verificar mensajes públicos (PublicMessage) según el RFC 9420. Esta funcionalidad es crucial para la interoperabilidad y seguridad del protocolo MLS, permitiendo a los miembros del grupo recibir y validar mensajes de difusión, incluyendo aquellos de remitentes externos.

Los cambios clave incluyen:
- La adición de la función `ProcessPublicMessage` en el módulo `group`, que se encarga de la verificación inicial y el despacho de mensajes públicos basados en su `ContentType` (Proposal, Commit).
- La extensión de la función `VerifyPublicMessage` para manejar la verificación de firmas de remitentes externos, utilizando la extensión `ExternalSenders` del `GroupContext`.
- La actualización de la verificación del `membership_tag` para incluir el `GroupContext` en el cálculo, conforme al RFC.
- La implementación de la deserialización de la extensión `ExternalSenders` para extraer las claves de firma de remitentes externos.
- La adición de un test de integración para asegurar que el `membership_tag` se incluye correctamente en los mensajes públicos de miembros y sobrevive el ciclo de serialización/deserialización.
- La adición de tests unitarios para `ProcessPublicMessage` que validan el almacenamiento de propuestas y el rechazo de commits públicos que contienen un `UpdatePath`.

Fixes #

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update

## How Has This Been Tested?
Agregué tests unitarios en `group/group_test.go` para verificar el procesamiento de propuestas y la correcta validación de membership tags en mensajes públicos. También incluí un test en `framing/framing_integration_test.go` para asegurar que los commits públicos con `UpdatePath` sean rechazados y que el `membership_tag` se maneje correctamente, como lo especifica el RFC.

author: stephanejouve
body:
## Summary

- Fix `calculate_weekly_transition()` treating Monday (first day of new week) as "completed week" instead of previous week
- Use `reference_date - 1 day` for calculation so Sunday evening and Monday morning yield the same transition
- Add regression test for the exact S084 incident scenario (Monday March 9 → S083 completed, not S084)

## Root cause

The function used `delta.days // 7` directly, which on Monday (week boundary) already counted the new week. On March 9 (Monday, first day of S084), it returned `week_completed=S084` instead of `S083`, causing the end-of-week workflow to run prematurely and generate S085 a full week early.

## Fix

Use yesterday's date (`reference_date - timedelta(days=1)`) to determine which week completed:
- Sunday: yesterday = Saturday (same week) → correct
- Monday: yesterday = Sunday (previous week) → now correct
- Mid-week: yesterday stays in same week → unchanged behavior

## Test plan

- [x] `test_calculate_weekly_transition_sunday` — Sunday gives S077→S078
- [x] `test_calculate_weekly_transition_monday` — Monday now gives S077→S078 (same as Sunday)
- [x] `test_calculate_weekly_transition_midweek` — Wednesday gives S078→S079
- [x] `test_calculate_weekly_transition_s084_monday_bug` — Regression: March 9 gives S083→S084
- [x] Full suite: 2059 passed

author: demonseed-jpg
body:
## Fixes #69

### Problem

The Docs Drift and Changelog checks always passed — even when docs were clearly stale. Two issues:

1. **Advisory only** — Both used `::warning::` annotations which are cosmetic. GitHub treats them as `success` conclusion. The Check Gate (or any branch protection) could never block based on these.

2. **Narrow coverage** — Docs Drift only checked 3 file patterns (routes, Cargo.toml members, config.rs). Changelog only triggered on `.rs` files. Workflow changes, Cargo.toml changes, and other significant modifications were invisible.

**Evidence:** PR #65 rewrote the entire auto-approve system (`.github/workflows/auto-approve.yml`) without updating `docs/PR-Reviews.md` or `CHANGELOG.md`. All checks passed with zero warnings.

### Fix

**Docs Drift:**
- Added: workflow files → `PR-Reviews.md` (blocking)
- Added: `deny.toml` → related docs (advisory)
- Changed from `::warning::` to `exit 1` for blocking drift

**Changelog:**
- Expanded trigger scope: `.rs`, `.yml` (workflows), `Cargo.toml`
- Changed from `::warning::` to `exit 1` when changelog missing
- Logs which file types triggered the requirement

**Docs updated:**
- `docs/PR-Reviews.md` — Docs Drift and Changelog rows updated from ⚠️ advisory to ✅ blocking
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entries for Check Gate and this fix

author: zoratu
body:
## Summary

- Add word boundary checking in `split_binary_op` to prevent partial operator matches
- Add test case for `\intersect` vs `\in` disambiguation

## Problem

When parsing binary operators, `\in` was incorrectly matching within `\intersect`:
- Expression: `seen \intersect Node`
- Incorrectly parsed as: left=`seen `, op=`\in`, right=`tersect Node`
- Error: "unexpected trailing tokens in expr: tersect Node"

This broke the LanguageFeatureMatrix spec which defines:
```tla
SeenIntersection == seen \intersect Node
```

## Solution

Add word boundary checking in `split_binary_op`: for operators that end with letters, ensure the next character is not also a letter. This prevents partial prefix matches.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_intersect_not_confused_with_in` test
- [x] Verified LanguageFeatureMatrix spec passes
- [x] Verified InitNextTemporalQuant spec passes
- [x] All 248 tests pass

## Summary
- Refined `pppFrameLerpPos` local/temporary typing and stack-local ordering in `src/pppLerpPos.cpp`.
- Reordered vector locals to better match original stack layout used by the PAL binary.
- Kept behavior unchanged while making source more plausible (`Vec*` field access for history samples).

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/pppLerpPos`
- Function: `pppFrameLerpPos`

## Progress evidence
Measured with:
`build/tools/objdiff-cli diff -p . -u main/pppLerpPos -o - pppFrameLerpPos`

- `pppFrameLerpPos` match: **96.21774% -> 96.29032%**
- Unit `.text` match (`main/pppLerpPos`): **96.89404% -> 96.95364%**
- No data or linkage regressions introduced.

## Plausibility rationale
- Changes preserve natural C/C++ structure and avoid compiler-coaxing hacks.
- Uses coherent vector semantics (`Vec` member access) and a plausible local-variable order rather than artificial symbol/offset tricks.
- No hardcoded symbol/address hacks or extern-only linkage shortcuts were introduced.

## Technical details
- Primary gain came from stack-local ordering alignment for vector temporaries used in the history shift/smoothing path.
- This reduced argument/stack-slot differences in objdiff and nudged function-level codegen closer to target while preserving control flow and data flow.

author: nrobi144
body:
## Summary

Two bugs in the Quartz NIP-46 remote signer library:

1. **NIP-44 HMAC key mutation** — `FixedKey.getEncoded()` returned a raw byte array reference. `javax.crypto.Mac.destroy()` zeroes the key material via `key.fill(0)`, corrupting the shared `saltPrefix` ("nip44-v2") in `Nip44v2` after first use. All subsequent NIP-44 decrypt operations fail with HMAC validation errors.

2. **NIP-46 connect response handling** — `connect()` used `PubKeyResponse::parse`, expecting a hex pubkey in the result. Per the NIP-46 spec and Amber maintainer feedback, connect never returns a pubkey — the response is `"ack"` (bunker://) or the secret string (nostrconnect://). Introduced `ConnectResponse` parser that checks `result`/`error` fields directly on the base `BunkerResponse` (matching Jackson deserialization behavior). `connect()` now returns `Unit` — callers call `getPublicKey()` separately as a domain concern.

## Changes

- **`FixedKey.getEncoded()`** — returns `key.copyOf()` instead of raw reference (prevents mutation)
- **`ConnectResponse`** — new parser that checks `result`/`error` fields directly on base `BunkerResponse`, not subclass pattern matching
- **`ConnectResult`** — sealed interface with `Ack` and `AlreadyConnected` (removed `PubKey` — connect never returns one)
- **`NostrSignerRemote.connect()`** — returns `Unit`, pure protocol handshake; callers call `getPublicKey()` separately

## Test plan

- [x] `Nip44v2JvmTest` — 5 tests: spec vectors, ECDH symmetry, encrypt/decrypt round-trip, cross-key-pair (NIP-46 pattern)
- [x] `ResponseParserTest` — 6 ConnectResponse tests (ack, secret string, already-connected, case-insensitive, error, no-result) + all other response parser tests (28 total)
- [x] All existing quartz + desktop tests pass

## Affected platforms

`FixedKey.kt` is in `jvmAndroid` source set — affects both Desktop JVM and Android.

### Submission Review Guidelines: - [x] I have followed the [WooCommerce Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/blob/trunk/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [WordPress Coding Standards](https://make.wordpress.org/core/handbook/best-practices/coding-standards/). - [x] I have checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/pulls) for the same update/change. - [x] I have reviewed my code for [security best practices](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/). ### Changes proposed in this Pull Request: When saving WooCommerce settings fields of type `password`, any `%` followed by two hex characters (e.g., `%Ec`, `%20`) is silently stripped. For example, the password `NlP4%EcCx}Na` becomes `NlP4Cx}Na`. This happens because `password` fields fall through to the `default` case in `WC_Admin_Settings::save_fields()`, which calls `wc_clean()` → `sanitize_text_field()`. WordPress's `sanitize_text_field()` intentionally strips `/%[a-f0-9]{2}/i` sequences as a security measure against URL-encoded HTML injection — appropriate for text labels, but destructive for passwords. This PR adds a dedicated `password` case that uses `wp_strip_all_tags()` instead. This still strips HTML tags (security) while preserving percent sequences that are legitimate password characters. A null guard ensures that when the field is absent from POST data, the stored value is left untouched rather than being overwritten with an empty string. Closes #62875 ### How to test the changes in this Pull Request: 1. Go to **WooCommerce → Settings → any tab** (e.g., Payments, or a custom settings tab from an extension). 2. Find or register a field of type `password`. 3. Enter a value containing `%` followed by two hex characters, e.g., `NlP4%EcCx}Na` or `test%20value`. 4. Save settings. - [x] Verify the saved value matches exactly what was entered — no characters stripped. 5. Enter a value containing HTML tags, e.g., `boldpass%E0word`. 6. Save settings. - [x] Verify HTML tags are stripped but the `%E0` sequence is preserved (saved value: `boldpass%E0word`). 7. Enter a value with leading/trailing whitespace, e.g., ` spaced%20pass `. 8. Save settings. - [x] Verify whitespace is trimmed but `%20` is preserved (saved value: `spaced%20pass`). 9. Go to a core WooCommerce text setting (e.g., **Settings → General → Store Address**). 10. Enter a normal text value. - [x] Verify text fields still behave as before (no regression). ### Testing that has already taken place: - 4 PHPUnit tests covering: percent-sequence preservation, HTML tag stripping, whitespace trimming, and text field non-regression. - PHP linting (PHPCS) — clean. - PHPStan — clean. ### Milestone - [x] Automatically assign milestone for the **[next WooCommerce version](../blob/trunk/plugins/woocommerce/woocommerce.php#L6)** ### Changelog entry - [ ] Automatically create a changelog entry from the details below.

body:
## Summary
- Adds `dev_canary_release.yml` workflow that publishes canary releases from the `dev` branch
- Runs automatically **every Monday at 06:00 UTC** and supports **manual dispatch** on demand
- Integrates into `release_test.yml` so canary can also be triggered after load tests pass

## How it works
1. **Test gate** — runs basic test suite before any publishing
2. **Version computation** — strips `.devN` suffix from `pyproject.toml`, appends `.dev{YYYYMMDD}` (PEP 440 compliant)
3. **PyPI publish** — publishes as a pre-release (`pip install cognee --pre` or `pip install cognee==0.5.4.dev20260309`)
4. **Docker publish** — pushes `cognee/cognee:dev-canary` (rolling) + `cognee/cognee:0.5.4.dev20260309` (pinned)

## Usage

This pull request refactors and modularizes the system prompt construction logic for the agent runtime, centralizing prompt section rendering into reusable functions in `agent/prompt.rs`. It also improves configurability of the bootstrap context size, removes duplicated code, and makes the prompt-building process more maintainable and testable.

Key changes include:

**Prompt Section Refactoring and Centralization:**

- Extracted the logic for rendering each prompt section (e.g., safety, skills, workspace, project context, runtime, date/time) into dedicated functions such as `render_safety_section`, `render_skills_section`, `render_workspace_section`, `render_project_context_section`, `render_runtime_section`, and `render_datetime_section` in `agent/prompt.rs`. These are now used both in the prompt builder and channel system prompt generation, ensuring consistency and reducing duplication. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c59d98d08266753caab80b15988a0b3dfb4b10fe817622f0882091b2e5db41dL79-R84) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c59d98d08266753caab80b15988a0b3dfb4b10fe817622f0882091b2e5db41dL152-R178) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b1471d3e1f21b12d288a4ca091df162b50a263b00e9d35b5f608fcc6dd477217R36-L38) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b1471d3e1f21b12d288a4ca091df162b50a263b00e9d35b5f608fcc6dd477217L965-R960)

- Replaced inline/duplicated logic for loading and injecting workspace files (OpenClaw bootstrap files) with a single `render_project_context_section` function, which handles both AIEOS and OpenClaw formats, including file truncation and missing-file markers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c59d98d08266753caab80b15988a0b3dfb4b10fe817622f0882091b2e5db41dL173-R279) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b1471d3e1f21b12d288a4ca091df162b50a263b00e9d35b5f608fcc6dd477217L965-R960) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b1471d3e1f21b12d288a4ca091df162b50a263b00e9d35b5f608fcc6dd477217L1082-L1126) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b1471d3e1f21b12d288a4ca091df162b50a263b00e9d35b5f608fcc6dd477217L859-L891)

author: christianhg
body:
Adds a `+` combinator syntax for combining multiple marks on the same content.

`[strong+em:text]` is syntactic sugar for `[strong:[em:text]]` - it produces the same nested Mark AST but is much more readable when multiple marks apply to the same text.

Each mark in the chain can have its own mode prefix and attributes:

```
[strong+em:bold and italic]
[strong+@link href="url":bold link]
[strong+@comment+@link:text]
```

This came out of the PTE textspec migration where we found that overlapping annotations produced deeply nested, hard-to-read notation:

```
# Before (nesting)
P: [@link:foo ][strong:[@comment:[@link:bar]]][strong:[@link:new]][@link: baz]

# After (combinator)
P: [@link:foo ][strong+@comment+@link:bar][strong+@link:new][@link: baz]
```

The AST is unchanged - the combinator is purely syntactic sugar. The parser produces nested Mark nodes, and the serializer detects single-child mark chains and outputs the combinator form.

Changes:
- Lexer: added `PLUS` token type
- Parser: `parseMark()` now parses `+`-separated mark specs and builds nested marks from outside-in
- Serializer: detects single-child mark chains and serializes with `+` combinator
- Tests: parser, serializer, and roundtrip tests for the combinator
- README: documented the combinator syntax in the marks section

author: caohy1988
body:
## Summary

Proposes `bqx` — a new agent-native BigQuery CLI modeled after the [Google Workspace CLI (gws)](https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli) architecture. Combines three command domains under one tool:

- **`bqx <resource> <method>`** — Dynamic BigQuery API commands generated from the Discovery Document (like `gws` generates from Google API Discovery)
- **`bqx analytics <command>`** — Agent Analytics SDK commands (evaluate, get-trace, drift, insights, views)
- **`bqx ca <command>`** — Conversational Analytics integration (natural language queries via CA API, data agents, verified queries)

### Key design decisions

- **Rust CLI** with two-phase arg parsing (same architecture as `gws`)
- **Agent Skills** (SKILL.md format from agentskills.io) — 20+ skills across 4 categories (service, helper, persona, recipe), compatible with Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Codex
- **JSON-first output** with progressive disclosure (~100 tokens to discover, ~4K to activate)
- **Conversational Analytics data agent** with verified queries for agent analytics (error rate, latency, tool failures)
- **Model Armor integration** for prompt injection screening
- **3-phase roadmap:** Core CLI + Analytics (4wk) → Dynamic API + Skills (4wk) → CA integration (3wk)

### Relationship to existing PRD

The current PRD (PR #25) defines a Python CLI (`bq-agent-sdk`). This proposal positions that as a v1.0 stepping-stone — once `bqx` reaches v0.2, analytics commands migrate to `bqx analytics` and the Python CLI is deprecated.

## Test plan

- [ ] Review architecture alignment with `gws` CLI patterns
- [ ] Validate SKILL.md examples against agentskills.io spec
- [ ] Verify verified queries are syntactically valid BigQuery SQL
- [ ] Confirm CA API capabilities match documented usage

author: aabccd021
body:
## Summary

- Replace static `rust-toolchain` file with dynamic target selection in flake.nix
- Linux systems get their musl target for static builds
- Darwin systems get their native target

## Problem

The static `rust-toolchain` file listed all 6 cross-compilation targets:
- aarch64-apple-darwin
- aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
- x86_64-apple-darwin
- x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
- aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
- x86_64-unknown-linux-musl

This caused rust-overlay to bundle ALL targets into a single toolchain derivation, regardless of which system was building. Building on x86_64-linux required downloading/building `rust-std-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` even though it was never used.

## Solution

Dynamically select the target based on the system:
- Linux: use `pkgsStatic.stdenv.targetPlatform.rust.cargoShortTarget` (e.g., `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`)
- Darwin: use native target (e.g., `aarch64-apple-darwin`)

This reduces the toolchain closure size significantly by only including the target actually needed for each system.

author: jiteshdugar
body:
## Summary
Fixed potential errors when switching tables by validating that field IDs exist in the selected table before attempting to load records. This prevents stale field IDs stored in globalConfig from causing failures.

## Key Changes
- **BulkConvertTab.js**: Enhanced `fieldsToLoad` filter to validate both source and destination field IDs exist in the selected table using `getFieldByIdIfExists()`
- **UploadTab.js**: Added validation check for destination field ID existence before including it in record query options

## Implementation Details
Both changes follow the same pattern: before using a field ID from globalConfig to query records, we now verify that the field actually exists in the current table. This is important because:
- Users may switch between tables while the component is mounted
- globalConfig may retain stale field IDs from previous table selections
- Attempting to query non-existent fields would cause errors

The validation uses the existing `getFieldByIdIfExists()` method which safely returns undefined if the field doesn't exist, allowing the filter/conditional to gracefully handle the case.

author: marcelroozekrans
body:
## Summary
- **Lazy startup**: `CreateAsync` returns after `OpenSolutionAsync` (~200ms), compiles all projects in the background via `_warmupTask`
- **Parallel compilation**: Projects are compiled by dependency level using topological sort — independent projects compile concurrently via `Task.WhenAll`
- **Thread-safe**: `LoadedSolution.Compilations` uses `ConcurrentDictionary`, `_tracker` initialized under lock, warmup exceptions stored and re-thrown to callers
- **Parallel rebuilds**: `ForceReloadAsync` and `RebuildStaleProjects` also use parallel compilation

### Architecture
```
Phase 1 (~200ms): OpenSolutionAsync → return immediately
Phase 2 (background): Compile Level 0 (leaves) → Level 1 → ... → Level N (root)
Phase 3: GetResolver() awaits warmup if still running, then returns
```

### Changes (6 files, +301/-30)
- `SolutionLoader.cs` — Split into `OpenAsync` + `CompileAllParallelAsync`, added `GetCompilationLevels` topological sort with cycle detection
- `SolutionManager.cs` — Lazy startup with `_warmupTask`, error propagation via `_warmupException`, parallel ForceReload and RebuildStale
- `LoadedSolution.cs` — `IDictionary` → `ConcurrentDictionary`
- 3 new test files with 8 new tests (82 total, all passing)

## Test plan
- [x] All 82 unit tests pass (`dotnet test -c Release`)
- [x] Benchmarks run successfully — tool latencies within noise
- [x] Topological sort handles: linear chains, independent groups, circular refs, empty solutions

- Eliminate the broken two-step photo opening flow and remove empty/intermediate modal states so any zoomable image opens immediately with one click.

## Summary
Enhanced the font loading mechanism for the graffiti wall to ensure custom fonts are fully loaded before rendering, improving reliability and preventing potential rendering issues.

## Key Changes
- Added explicit `document.fonts.load()` calls for the three custom fonts used in graffiti rendering:
  - Sedgwick Ave Display
  - Permanent Marker
  - Impact
- These fonts are now force-loaded in parallel using `Promise.all()` before waiting for `document.fonts.ready`
- Updated the comment to better reflect the intent of forcing font loads

## Implementation Details
The change uses the Font Loading API to explicitly load each font variant (bold 80px) before proceeding with grid rendering. This ensures that all custom fonts are available in the document's font cache, preventing potential layout shifts or fallback font rendering that could occur if fonts loaded asynchronously during the rendering process.

author: madmax983
body:
**Threat:** The `intersect_rect` function in `experiments/chimera-tardis/src/safe_gl.rs` allowed negative width or height values to be passed to saturating addition, potentially resulting in underflow/overflow or negative dimensions being passed to `glScissor`, which could invoke Undefined Behavior depending on driver implementation. This issue was also replicated in `impossible-explorer`, `alloc-tardis`, and `trace-tardis`.
**Defense:** Explicitly clamped `w` and `h` inputs via `.max(0)` before calculating the intersection bounds to ensure mathematical soundness and prevent negative `glScissor` arguments.
**Severity:** Medium - could trigger OpenGL driver panics or undefined behavior.
**Verification:** Added `test_intersect_rect_negative_dimensions` unit test.

author: sorayaormazabalmayo
body: This PR implements persistent D-Bus signal monitoring at the adapter level to detect abrupt disconnections. The `connectHandler` callback was not being invoked when Bluetooth devices disconnected abruptly (e.g., device powered off, out of range, battery died) on Linux. It only worked for planned disconnections via `Device.Disconnect()`. This created an inconsistency with the Darwin implementation, which correctly detects all disconnections through CoreBluetooth's `DidDisconnectPeripheral` delegate method.

author: kwesiadom875-arch
body:
💡 What: 
Added crucial accessibility and UX improvements to the `ConfirmationModal` component. This includes auto-focusing the cancel button, adding `Escape` key and clickaway support, setting `role="dialog"`, and mapping ARIA attributes to the title and message. It also locks body scroll while the modal is open.

🎯 Why: 
Modals are disruptive by nature. For destructive actions (like deleting an item), it's a critical UX failure to not auto-focus the safe option ("Cancel") or to trap keyboard users inside without an easy way out (like pressing Escape). Furthermore, screen readers need semantic context to understand that a dialog has opened and what it's asking.

📸 Before/After: 
Visually, the modal appears the same, but the Cancel button now immediately receives a focus ring upon opening. 

♿ Accessibility: 
- `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` tell screen readers they are trapped in a modal context.
- `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` explicitly read the prompt to visually impaired users.
- The `Escape` key listener enables standard keyboard-only dismissal.
- Auto-focusing "Cancel" prevents accidental "Enter" key presses from triggering destructive actions.
