author: lukinovec
body:
This PR adds the `toRoute()` method override to `TenancyUrlGenerator`. `toRoute()` now attempts to find a  tenant equivalent of the passed route (= a route with the same name as the passed one, but with the tenant prefix) and generates URL for the tenant route. This behavior can be bypassed using the bypass parameter, like with the `route()` method override `TenancyUrlGenerator` had until now.

The primary reason for adding this is that Livewire v4 no longer uses the `route()` helper (which automatically prefixes the passed route name because of the override in `TenancyUrlGenerator`) in `Livewire::getUpdateUri()`. Now, it uses `toRoute()` (https://github.com/livewire/livewire/commit/544aa3dfb8195f342ef0adbf179139841ad817b7#diff-e7609f8b0a60bde5a85067803d4e2f08f235c7cee9225a51ea67a85ff9a1d694R52), which didn't automatically swap the route for its 'tenant.'-prefixed equivalent in tenant context (until now). So for the Livewire integration to work with path identification, we need to override `toRoute()` as described.

The `temporarySignedRoute()` override got removed because `temporarySignedRoute()` calls `route()` under the hood, there's no need to specifically override `temporarySignedRoute()`.

> Note: Browsing old convos, it seems like the `temporarySignedRoute()` override was needed to make Livewire file uploads work with path identification, but it's not needed anymore. TenancyUrlGenerator had some changes since then, and now, I can't see the _exact_ reason why we needed the override (`temporarySignedRoute()` uses `route()` under the hood, so the only thing that should really matter is overriding `route()`/`toRoute()`). It was likely a leftover from some older implementation.

The `route()` override got simplified. Since `route()` uses `toRoute()` under the hood, the `route()` override only has to have the prefixing logic. The rest is delegated to `toRoute()`.

> Note: Even though we override `toRoute()` now which `route()` uses for generating the URLs, we still need to override `route()` for its `$this->routes->getByName($name)` call to receive the prefixed name. For example, if `route()` wasn't overridden, and we only had one route: `tenant.foo` (no central `foo` route), and we'd call `route('foo')`, we'd get an exception saying that route "foo" wasn't found, even if automatic route name prefixing was enabled and `toRoute()` was overridden. With the `route()` override, `route('foo')` acts as if we passed 'tenant.foo' instead of 'foo'.

Comments in TenancyUrlGenerator and UrlGeneratorBootstrapper got updated to be more accurate. All _intentionally_ affected methods are listed in TenancyUrlGenerator's docblock.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Unified URL generation so route-name prefixing and tenant-parameter injection apply consistently across more URL entry points; bypass handling now reliably skips these behaviors.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified wording describing how tenant parameters are included in generated links.

* **Tests**
  * Added tests verifying prefixed-route selection, tenant-parameter injection for unnamed routes, and bypass behavior.

author: sotashimozono
body:
# Description

I implemented `loginner` and `logdot` methods.
Fixes #1552 

In the previous implementation for MPS/MPO, the contraction order was well-defined, and we utilized a specialized method to compute the inner product in the logarithmic scale.

For general ITensor objects, however, the optimal contraction sequence is not uniquely determined. Therefore, I have implemented a straightforward fallback as follows:
```julia
inner(y::ITensor, x::ITensor) = (dag(y) * x)[]
loginner(A::ITensor, B::ITensor) = log(complex(inner(A, B)))
```

example code:

```julia
i = Index(2)
j = Index(2)
A = random_itensor(ElType, i', j', i, j)
x = random_itensor(ElType, i, j)
y = random_itensor(ElType, i, j)


val2 = inner(x, y)
val3 = inner(x', A, y)

@assert loginner(x, y) ≈ log(complex(val2))
@assert logdot(x, y) ≈ log(complex(val2))
```

# How Has This Been Tested?

I added testcode in `test_itensor.jl`

author: copilot
body:
Several combat UX and correctness issues: healing items were silently targeting enemies and not refreshing the HP bar UI; Sentinel had no tooltip and did nothing when used as a skill; portrait mode caused party icons to overlap; and VictoryScene content could overflow off-screen with many skill gains.

## Combat system

- **`useItem`**: emit `combat:heal` after HP/MP restore so the UI bar refreshes immediately (was consumed silently)
- **`applySkillEffect`**: add `'stance'` type handler — Sentinel now correctly applies its status to the actor
- Self-targeting skills (e.g. Sentinel) skip target-selection entirely and execute immediately

## Combat UI — target selection

- `enterTargetMode` now checks item/skill target type; for `single_ally` actions, allies are listed first so the cursor defaults to a party member rather than an enemy:

```typescript
const preferAlly = itemDef?.target === 'single_ally';
this.targetList = preferAlly ? [...allies, ...foes] : [...foes, ...allies];
```

## Combat UI — tooltips

- `buildMenuItems` accepts an optional `tooltips[]` parameter; hovering any skill or item entry updates the help-text bar with its description
- `buildSkillMenu` / `buildItemMenu` pass descriptions from `skills.json` / `items.json`
- Tooltip hint strings extracted to module-level constants (`HELP_TEXT_SKILL`, `HELP_TEXT_ITEM`, `HELP_TEXT_DEFAULT`)

## Portrait icon spacing

- `PLAYER_SPREAD` and `ENEMY_SPREAD` now enforce `(iconWidth + 6) × count` as a minimum, preventing icon overlap on narrow screens regardless of party size

## VictoryScene overflow

- `lineH` is capped dynamically: `Math.min(height * 0.072, availableH / estimatedLines)`, where `estimatedLines` is computed from actual render content (items found, skills learned, etc.)
- "Continue" prompt moved from `height * 0.9` → `0.93` for extra clearance

Our migration guides can help guide you through a list of mappings and some notable differences between the two tools.

Standard presubmit tests are run as part of this CL's workflow. **If you need to target an additional test workflow or require assistance with testing, please let us know.**

author: calgooon
body:
### This pull request:

Proposes a new standard by creating a new markdown file in the appropriate directory and requests discussion and assignment of a BRC number

### Summary

Adds BRC-115: a backward-compatible extension to [BRC-105](./payments/0105.md) that introduces `multipart/form-data` as an alternative transport for `x-bsv-payment` data when BEEF transactions exceed HTTP header size limits.

**Problem:** BEEF transactions grow cumulatively with unconfirmed ancestor chain depth. Applications doing rapid sequential payments (chaining hundreds or thousands of transactions before block confirmation) produce single-transaction BEEF payloads that exceed HTTP header limits within minutes — empirical measurements show 155.7 KB after 5 minutes of chaining, surpassing Cloudflare Workers' 128 KB header limit.

**Solution:** Client and server negotiate transport via a new `x-bsv-payment-transports` header in the 402 response. When payment JSON exceeds header limits and the server advertises `multipart` support, the client sends payment as a `multipart/form-data` body part. Payment JSON structure, authentication, and verification are unchanged.

**Key properties:**
- Fully backward compatible — small payments continue using header transport
- Header transport is not deprecated
- Same payment JSON format, same BRC-103 auth flow
- Server detects transport via `Content-Type` inspection
- Three production implementations exist (Rust server, Rust client, Python client)

This was discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin-sv/ts-sdk/pull/167 where @sirdeggen suggested writing it up as a BRC.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a service that ingests SOL token discovery webhooks and automatically monitors 1-minute OHLCV to detect short-term trade opportunities using EMA9/EMA20 and RSI(9).  
- Implement a robust market-state-driven strategy switcher (trend/range/down) with a 2-tick confirmation rule to avoid frequent flips.  
- Deliver actionable signals via outbound webhooks and a simple dashboard for operators to view monitored tokens and signal history.

### Description
- Added a FastAPI application (`app/main.py`) exposing `POST /webhook/add-token`, `GET /dashboard`, and `GET /healthz`, plus a background loop that runs the monitor every 60 seconds.  
- Implemented `GeckoClient` to fetch CoinGecko Pro On-Chain OHLCV and token metadata, `StrategyEngine` to classify market state and evaluate `BUY/ADD/SELL/HOLD` rules (EMA9/EMA20/RSI9), and `MonitorService` to orchestrate token lifecycle and signalling.  
- Implemented `SignalDispatcher` to forward BUY/ADD to the buy webhook and SELL to the sell webhook, whitelist→blacklist exit rules (FDV < 20,000 or age > 48h) with pre-exit SELL when holding, and a Jinja2 dashboard template (`templates/dashboard.html`) showing tokens and signal logs.  
- Added project metadata (`pyproject.toml`), basic unit tests (`tests/test_engine.py`), documentation (`README.md`), and `.gitignore`.

### Testing
- `python -m compileall app tests` completed successfully and validated module compilation.  
- `pytest` execution in this environment failed due to missing runtime dependencies (`httpx`, `fastapi`) which could not be installed here because package installation is blocked by network/proxy restrictions.  
- `pip install -e '.[dev]'` also failed in this environment due to the same network/proxy limitation preventing dependency installation; the code and tests run normally once dependencies are installed in a network-enabled environment.

body:
💡 **What:** Optimized the `updateUI` method in `src/main.js` to prevent redundant DOM writes. A new `_setVal` helper was introduced to verify if an input's value has actually changed and if it is not currently focused before performing an assignment.

🎯 **Why:** The `updateUI` method is called frequently (potentially every frame at 60fps) during rendering and interactions. Redundant DOM `value` assignments are expensive and can trigger unnecessary browser layout/paint operations.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Using a Node.js benchmark mocking the `updateUI` logic:
- **Baseline:** 7,000 DOM assignments in 1,000 calls (for 7 inputs) when values were stable.
- **Optimized:** 7 DOM assignments in 1,000 calls (initial updates only).
- **Change:** ~99.9% reduction in DOM write operations when UI values are not changing.

author: copilot
body:
The project had minimal ESLint config, no Prettier, an untyped custom server, undocumented env vars, and several dependency CVEs including an authorization bypass and DoS in Next.js 14.x.

## Security

- **`next` 14.2.3 → 15.3.9** — fixes authorization bypass (middleware, CVE affects < 14.2.25), cache poisoning (< 14.2.10), and HTTP request deserialization DoS (affects all 13.x/14.x, patched in 15.0.8)
- **`axios` 1.6.8 → 1.8.2** — fixes SSRF/credential leakage via absolute URL (< 1.8.2)

## ESLint

Expanded `.eslintrc.json` from the bare `next/core-web-vitals` extend to include `@typescript-eslint/recommended` with explicit rules:

```json
{
  "extends": ["next/core-web-vitals", "plugin:@typescript-eslint/recommended"],
  "rules": {
    "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "warn",
    "@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": ["error", { "argsIgnorePattern": "^_", "varsIgnorePattern": "^_" }],
    "@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports": ["warn", { "prefer": "type-imports" }],
    "prefer-const": "error",
    "no-console": ["warn", { "allow": ["warn", "error"] }]
  }
}
```

Fixed all resulting violations across the codebase: `let` → `const`, removed unused imports/variables, replaced inline `require("axios")` calls with module-level ES imports.

## Next.js 15 migration

Next.js 15 makes `params` async. Updated all 5 dynamic route pages to `async` functions that `await params`, with proper typed signatures replacing `any`:

```tsx
// Before (Next.js 14)
export default function Page({ params }: any) {
  return <FormContent uuid={params.uuid} />;
}

// After (Next.js 15)
export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ uuid: string }> }) {
  const { uuid } = await params;
  return <FormContent uuid={uuid} />;
}
```

## TypeScript server

Converted `server.js` → `server.ts` with proper types (`IncomingMessage`, `ServerResponse`) and reads `NODE_PORT`/`NODE_HOSTNAME` from env instead of hardcoded values.

## New tooling

- **Prettier**: added `.prettierrc`; added `format` / `format:check` scripts
- **Type checking**: added `type-check` script (`tsc --noEmit`)
- **Custom server runner**: added `server` script using `tsx server.ts`
- **New devDeps**: `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`, `@typescript-eslint/parser`, `tsx`, `prettier`

## Environment docs

Rewrote `.env.example` with section headers and inline comments for every variable; fixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIL_SERVIC` typo → `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAIL_SERVICE` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_FlUTTER_KEY` → `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLUTTERWAVE_KEY`.

author: copilot
body:
`useRefObjectAsForwardedRef` had a bug where `useImperativeHandle` would re-call on every render, risking infinite loops when combined with state-setting callback refs. This PR replaces it with a `useCombinedRefs` hook that uses a callback ref as its trigger, so refs are only updated when the target actually changes.

### Key improvements over `useRefObjectAsForwardedRef`

- **No infinite loop risk**: callback-ref-based trigger avoids re-firing on every render
- **React 19 compatible**: handles cleanup functions returned by callback refs; remains React 18 compatible
- **Accepts `undefined`**: works ergonomically with optional React 19 `ref` props
- **Order-agnostic**: no silent failure if argument order is swapped
- **Supports two callback refs**: internal callback refs can coexist with external refs
- **Better types**: reduces need for casting

### Usage

```tsx
// React 18
const Example = forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement>((props, forwardedRef) => {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  const combinedRef = useCombinedRefs(forwardedRef, ref)
  return <button ref={combinedRef} />
})

// React 19
const Example = ({ref: externalRef}: {ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>}) => {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
  const combinedRef = useCombinedRefs(externalRef, ref)
  return <button ref={combinedRef} />
}
```

For more than two refs: `useCombinedRefs(refA, useCombinedRefs(refB, refC))`

### Migration from `useRefObjectAsForwardedRef`

```diff
  const ref = useRef(null)

- useRefObjectAsForwardedRef(forwardedRef, ref)
+ const combinedRef = useCombinedRefs(forwardedRef, ref)

- return <div ref={ref} />
+ return <div ref={combinedRef} />
```

`useRefObjectAsForwardedRef` is deprecated (not removed) to allow a gradual migration; it will be deleted in the next major release.

### Changelog

#### New

- `useCombinedRefs` hook

#### Changed

- `useRefObjectAsForwardedRef` deprecated with inline migration instructions
- Migrated `ButtonBase`, `Dialog`, `Heading`, `Link`, `Overlay`, `PageLayout`, `AutocompleteInput`, `AutocompleteOverlay`, `TextInputWithTokens`, and `deprecated/Dialog` to `useCombinedRefs`

#### Removed

### Rollout strategy

- [ ] Patch release
- [x] Minor release
- [ ] Major release; if selected, include a written rollout or migration plan
- [ ] None; if selected, include a brief description as to why

### Testing & Reviewing

Unit tests cover: forwarding to object refs, callback refs, React 19 cleanup callbacks, null/undefined handling, and combined callback+object ref scenarios.

### Merge checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Added/updated documentation
- [ ] Added/updated previews (Storybook)
- [ ] Changes are [SSR compatible](https://github.com/primer/react/blob/main/contributor-docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#ssr-compatibility)
- [ ] Tested in Chrome
- [ ] Tested in Firefox

author: copilot
body:
The world creation seed field was still not receiving actual keyboard text input before gameplay started. This updates the pre-game-loop UI path to use Dear ImGui’s native text input flow directly instead of the seed-specific keypress fallback added in the prior attempt.

- **Native SDL → ImGui event path**
  - Forward raw `SDL_Event` payloads from the SDL backend into Dear ImGui during menu/event processing.
  - Enable SDL text input for the windowed backend so `SDL_TEXTINPUT`, backspace, and enter reach ImGui as real text/edit events.

- **Submit-aware ImGui text input API**
  - Extend the UI backend with a submit-aware text input call returning:
    - whether text changed
    - whether Enter submitted
    - the updated value
  - Expose a matching C++ ImGui binding using `ImGuiInputTextFlags_EnterReturnsTrue`.

- **World creation screen cleanup**
  - Remove the seed field’s manual `InputManager` fallback for digits/backspace/delete/return.
  - Make the world creation seed box depend on ImGui text input state exclusively, so the pre-game-loop menu behaves like a real ImGui input widget.

- **UI backend integration**
  - Add a platform-event forwarding hook to `UIManager` / `ImGuiBackend` so menu screens can receive native input without inventing a separate pre-loop input path.

- **Focused coverage**
  - Update tests to reflect the intended behavior:
    - raw menu keypresses no longer emulate seed editing
    - direct ImGui-style submit can start world generation
    - platform events are forwarded from the runner into the UI backend

Example of the new backend contract:

```python
changed, submitted, new_text = self._backend.input_text_state(
    "##seed", self._seed_text, 64
)

if changed:
    self._seed_text = new_text
    self._status_message = ""

if self._backend.button("Generate World", button_width, 50) or submitted:
    ...
```

### Update [beautifulsoup4](https://pypi.org/project/beautifulsoup4) from **4.6.3** to **4.14.3**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.11.1
   ```
   This release was done to ensure that the unit tests are packaged along
with the released source. There are no functionality changes in this
release, but there are a few other packaging changes:

* The Japanese and Korean translations of the documentation are included.
* The changelog is now packaged as CHANGELOG, and the license file is
  packaged as LICENSE. NEWS.txt and COPYING.txt are still present,
  but may be removed in the future.
* TODO.txt is no longer packaged, since a TODO is not relevant for released
  code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.11.0
   ```
   * Ported unit tests to use pytest.

* Added special string classes, RubyParenthesisString and RubyTextString,
  to make it possible to treat ruby text specially in get_text() calls.
  [bug=1941980]

* It's now possible to customize the way output is indented by
  providing a value for the 'indent' argument to the Formatter
  constructor. The 'indent' argument works very similarly to the
  argument of the same name in the Python standard library's
  json.dump() function. [bug=1955497]

* If the charset-normalizer Python module
  (https://pypi.org/project/charset-normalizer/) is installed, Beautiful
  Soup will use it to detect the character sets of incoming documents.
  This is also the module used by newer versions of the Requests library.
  For the sake of backwards compatibility, chardet and cchardet both take
  precedence if installed. [bug=1955346]

* Added a workaround for an lxml bug
  (https://bugs.launchpad.net/lxml/+bug/1948551) that causes
  problems when parsing a Unicode string beginning with BYTE ORDER MARK.
  [bug=1947768]

* Issue a warning when an HTML parser is used to parse a document that
  looks like XML but not XHTML. [bug=1939121]

* Do a better job of keeping track of namespaces as an XML document is
  parsed, so that CSS selectors that use namespaces will do the right
  thing more often. [bug=1946243]

* Some time ago, the misleadingly named "text" argument to find-type
  methods was renamed to the more accurate "string." But this supposed
  "renaming" didn't make it into important places like the method
  signatures or the docstrings. That's corrected in this
  version. "text" still works, but will give a DeprecationWarning.
  [bug=1947038]

* Fixed a crash when pickling a BeautifulSoup object that has no
  tree builder. [bug=1934003]

* Fixed a crash when overriding multi_valued_attributes and using the
  html5lib parser. [bug=1948488]

* Standardized the wording of the MarkupResemblesLocatorWarning
  warnings to omit untrusted input and make the warnings less
  judgmental about what you ought to be doing. [bug=1955450]

* Removed support for the iconv_codec library, which doesn't seem
  to exist anymore and was never put up on PyPI. (The closest
  replacement on PyPI, iconv_codecs, is GPL-licensed, so we can't use
  it--it's also quite old.)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.10.0
   ```
   * This is the first release of Beautiful Soup to only support Python
  3. I dropped Python 2 support to maintain support for newer versions
  (58 and up) of setuptools. See:
  https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/2769 [bug=1942919]

* The behavior of methods like .get_text() and .strings now differs
  depending on the type of tag. The change is visible with HTML tags
  like <script>, <style>, and <template>. Starting in 4.9.0, methods
  like get_text() returned no results on such tags, because the
  contents of those tags are not considered 'text' within the document
  as a whole.

  But a user who calls script.get_text() is working from a different
  definition of 'text' than a user who calls div.get_text()--otherwise
  there would be no need to call script.get_text() at all. In 4.10.0,
  the contents of (e.g.) a <script> tag are considered 'text' during a
  get_text() call on the tag itself, but not considered 'text' during
  a get_text() call on the tag's parent.

  Because of this change, calling get_text() on each child of a tag
  may now return a different result than calling get_text() on the tag
  itself. That's because different tags now have different
  understandings of what counts as 'text'. [bug=1906226] [bug=1868861]

* NavigableString and its subclasses now implement the get_text()
  method, as well as the properties .strings and
  .stripped_strings. These methods will either return the string
  itself, or nothing, so the only reason to use this is when iterating
  over a list of mixed Tag and NavigableString objects. [bug=1904309]

* The 'html5' formatter now treats attributes whose values are the
  empty string as HTML boolean attributes. Previously (and in other
  formatters), an attribute value must be set as None to be treated as
  a boolean attribute. In a future release, I plan to also give this
  behavior to the 'html' formatter. Patch by Isaac Muse. [bug=1915424]

* The 'replace_with()' method now takes a variable number of arguments,
  and can be used to replace a single element with a sequence of elements.
  Patch by Bill Chandos. [rev=605]

* Corrected output when the namespace prefix associated with a
  namespaced attribute is the empty string, as opposed to
  None. [bug=1915583]

* Performance improvement when processing tags that speeds up overall
  tree construction by 2%. Patch by Morotti. [bug=1899358]

* Corrected the use of special string container classes in cases when a
  single tag may contain strings with different containers; such as
  the <template> tag, which may contain both TemplateString objects
  and Comment objects. [bug=1913406]

* The html.parser tree builder can now handle named entities
  found in the HTML5 spec in much the same way that the html5lib
  tree builder does. Note that the lxml HTML tree builder doesn't handle
  named entities this way. [bug=1924908]

* Added a second way to pass specify encodings to UnicodeDammit and
  EncodingDetector, based on the order of precedence defined in the
  HTML5 spec, starting at:
  https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-with-a-known-character-encoding

  Encodings in 'known_definite_encodings' are tried first, then
  byte-order-mark sniffing is run, then encodings in 'user_encodings'
  are tried. The old argument, 'override_encodings', is now a
  deprecated alias for 'known_definite_encodings'.

  This changes the default behavior of the html.parser and lxml tree
  builders, in a way that may slightly improve encoding
  detection but will probably have no effect. [bug=1889014]

* Improve the warning issued when a directory name (as opposed to
  the name of a regular file) is passed as markup into the BeautifulSoup
  constructor. [bug=1913628]
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.9.3
   ```
   * Implemented a significant performance optimization to the process of
  searching the parse tree. Patch by Morotti. [bug=1898212]
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.9.2
   ```
   * Fixed a bug that caused too many tags to be popped from the tag
  stack during tree building, when encountering a closing tag that had
  no matching opening tag. [bug=1880420]

* Fixed a bug that inconsistently moved elements over when passing
  a Tag, rather than a list, into Tag.extend(). [bug=1885710]

## Summary

- Add Step Functions pipeline for automated CRE document processing: split PDF/Excel → OCR (DeepSeek) or convert to markdown → classify document type (Bedrock Claude) → extract structured JSON → save to S3
- Support both PDF (.pdf) and Excel (.xlsx/.xls) files via Choice state routing in Step Functions
- PDF path: SplitPdf → Map(ConvertToImage → OcrPage via DeepSeek ALB → ClassifyAndExtract via Bedrock)
- Excel path: ExcelToSheets (openpyxl/xlrd → markdown tables) → Map(ClassifyAndExtract via Bedrock)
- New CDK `PipelineStack` with 3 Docker Lambdas (split-pdf, pdf-to-image, excel-to-text), 4 TypeScript Lambdas (ocr-page, classify-extract, save-results, start-pipeline), IAM roles, and state machine
- API Gateway `POST /pipeline/process` endpoint to trigger pipeline

author: h7kz
body:
## Summary

  - `preparePool` and `uploadPool` both used index `0`, which is the same pool object
    as `connectPool`. All tasks were therefore added to a single pool and the intended
    connect → prepare → upload ordering was not enforced by the framework. Tasks
    reading `"token"` and `"versionUpload"` from process data could run before those
    values were stored. Fixed by assigning `preparePool` to index `1` and `uploadPool`
    to index `2`.
  - `NAME`, `VERSION`, and `DESCRIPTION` were used from `CommonPropertyKey` without
    being checked for absence. If any of these were unset, `StringBuilder.append(null)`
    would produce the literal string `"null"` in the Hangar release notes or version
    name. Added them to the `isAbsentAndAnnounce` guard so the platform fails fast
    with a clear message instead.

author: tglunde
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses cache inconsistencies (Issue #177) by aligning relation rename and replace behavior with the dbt-adapters framework, and crucially, by overriding the default table and view materializations to perform atomic replacements.

## Changes Made
- **Materialization Overrides (Cache Inconsistency Fix):** 
  - Overrode the default `table` and `view` materializations to exclusively use atomic `CREATE OR REPLACE` operations.
  - *Context:* This bypasses the default framework behavior of using intermediate and backup relations (the "rename swap" pattern) for standard tables and views. Skipping the backup/rename lifecycle is essential for Exasol to prevent the dbt adapter cache from falling out of sync with the database, which was the root cause of the cache inconsistencies.
- **Relation Management:** Updated `ExasolRelation` to declare tables and views as `renameable_relations` and `replaceable_relations`.
- **Per-Type Macros:** Implemented per-type rename, replace, and drop macros (`exasol__get_rename_table_sql`, `exasol__drop_view`, etc.).
- **Other Materialization Updates:**
  - Migrated the incremental materialization full-refresh path to use the framework's intermediate/backup/rename swap pattern.
  - Replaced legacy relation drops in snapshot `exasol__post_snapshot` with safe `drop_relation_if_exists()`.
- **Legacy Cleanup:** Removed legacy `exasol__rename_relation` and `exasol__drop_relation` macros to ensure the new framework dispatch path is used.
- **Testing & Docs:** Added unit test coverage for `can_be_renamed` and `can_be_replaced` properties in `ExasolRelation`, and included specs and design documents.

### Motivation
- Address inconsistent and silent `try/except` patterns that hide parsing and persistence errors and make debugging hard.
- Provide consistent user-facing feedback and logs when persisted state or uploaded files cannot be parsed or trigger rebuild failures.

### Description
- Added a shared helper `_read_tabular_with_fallbacks(file, dataset_name, preferred_sheet)` in `data_processor.py` that tries a named Excel sheet, first Excel sheet, then CSV, rewinds file-like objects between attempts, logs each fallback failure, and raises a contextual `ValueError` if all attempts fail.
- Updated `parse_budget(...)` and `parse_families(...)` to use the new `_read_tabular_with_fallbacks` helper to replace nested `try/except` fallbacks with a single consistent mechanism.
- Enhanced `persistence.py` by adding a module `logger`, logging exceptions per-key when loading persisted state, collecting load errors and surfacing a user `st.warning` if some keys failed to load, and logging plus showing a user-facing `st.error` when KPI rebuild fails after load.
- Improved error messages and logging so failures include context (which fallback failed and why) to aid production debugging without changing existing fallback behavior.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall app.py data_processor.py persistence.py` to ensure files compile successfully and reported no compilation errors.

body:
## Summary
- Fixes the `arch` variable being incorrect when cross-building (e.g. building for Intel on an ARM Mac by pointing `JAVA_HOME` to an x86_64 JDK)
- Introduces `jdkArch()` which reads the `OS_ARCH` property from the configured JDK's `release` file instead of relying on `System.getProperty("os.arch")` (which reflects the Gradle daemon's host architecture)
- Updates electron-builder config generation, artifact naming, and resource bundling to use the target JDK's architecture

## Details
The root cause was that `currentArch` uses `System.getProperty("os.arch")`, which returns the **host** architecture (the machine running the build), not the **target** architecture. When cross-building via Rosetta 2 with an Intel JDK, the JDK itself correctly reports `x86_64` in its `release` file, but the Gradle daemon still reports `aarch64`.

The new `jdkArch(javaHome)` function reads the JDK's `release` file to get the actual target architecture, falling back to `currentArch` if the file cannot be parsed.

Fixes #71

## Test plan
- [ ] Build for the native architecture and verify artifact names contain the correct arch
- [ ] Cross-build on an ARM Mac using an Intel JDK (`JAVA_HOME` pointing to x86_64 JDK) and verify artifact names contain `x64` instead of `arm64`
- [ ] Verify electron-builder YAML config contains the correct `arch` field

author: copilot
body:
When master was merged in, the new search functionality added code that bypassed the existing cached frame accessor pattern, creating inconsistencies. Three issues are addressed:

## MainFramePrototype.lua

- `SetSearchQuery()` was doing raw `_G[self:GetName() .. "List"]` and `_G[listFrame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar"]` lookups — now uses `GetListFrame()` / `GetListScrollBar()`
- `RevealSearchMatch()` was accessing the FOV scrollbar via hardcoded `_G["DBM_GUI_OptionsFramePanelContainerFOVScrollBar"]` — now uses `GetContainerScrollBar()`

## DBM-GUI.lua

`typeFlags` was a nested table of flag-objects requiring 3 conditionals per element:

```lua
-- Before: 3 checks per element in the loop
typeFlags = { statusbar = { texture = true }, font = { font = true }, sound = { sound = true } }
if typeFlag.texture then result[i].texture = true end
if typeFlag.font then result[i].font = true end
if typeFlag.sound then result[i].sound = true end
```

Simplified to direct key-name strings — one table field assignment per element:

```lua
-- After: single assignment
typeFlags = { statusbar = "texture", font = "font", sound = "sound" }
result[i][flagKey] = true
```

`tinsert(result, ins)` was also sitting outside the `if flagKey then` block, diverging from the original insert-only-if-flagged semantics. Moved inside.

author: jcogilvie
body:
### Description of your changes

This PR fixes an issue where `crossplane-diff` fails when function packages are referenced by SHA256 digest instead of tag.

**Problem:**
When a function uses a digest reference like `function-go-templating@sha256:54726c28b78f...`, the container name generation produced invalid Docker container names containing the `@` character, which Docker rejects:

```
Error response from daemon: Invalid container name (...@sha256-...), only [a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-] are allowed
```

**Solution:**
1. Handle SHA256 digest references specially - extract the function name and truncate the digest to 12 characters (similar to Docker short image IDs)
2. Enforce a 63-character limit on container names (DNS hostname compatibility) with hash-based truncation for uniqueness

**Example transformations:**
- `function-go-templating@sha256:54726c28b78f51a7e88b87db33de79721d8be60890b71dad96276aea4a3397d1`
  → `function-go-templating-54726c28b78f-comp-a1b2c3d4`
- Long function names are truncated with a hash suffix to maintain uniqueness while staying under 63 chars

**Test coverage:**
- Unit tests for SHA256 digest handling, length constraints, and truncation stability
- Integration test (`SHA256DigestFunctionReference`) validates the full flow with a real function referenced by digest

Fixes #245

author: azezik
body:
### Motivation
- The implementation drifted panel-first / bbox-first despite the intended visual-first architecture, causing visual signals to be underweighted and overlays to present bbox geometry as primary truth. 
- Seed/precompute artifacts were often created without `imageData`, biasing downstream region proposals toward text/layout primitives. 
- Phase 0 must apply the smallest safe corrections to make visual signals first-class, add a geometry-faithful debug layer, and de-emphasize panel as a primary ontology without broad rewrites.

### Description
- Added design-alignment documentation and a phased correction plan in `docs/wrokitvision-design-alignment-audit.md` and `docs/wrokitvision-visual-first-correction-plan.md` to record findings, scope, and Phase 0 goals. 
- Made `imageData` first-class in the seed path by passing `imageData` from `createSeedArtifacts(...)` into `buildMaps(...)` so precompute/mapping can use pixels when available. 
- Introduced a geometry-faithful debug overlay layer (`regionGeometryOverlay` / `region-geometry-truth`) while retaining a bbox compatibility overlay (`region-proposals-bbox-debug`), and wired both into upload analysis debug artifacts. 
- Propagated richer geometry through the stack: `detect-region-proposals` now plants `contour` / `hull` / `rotatedRect` descriptors (with bbox fallback), `vision/types` preserves these descriptors, `precomputed`→legacy adapter exposes geometry-faithful `visualRegionLayer` with role metadata, and `detect-surface-candidates` de-emphasizes `panel` as a primary type while adding `panelLike` as derived metadata.

### Testing
- Added `test/wrokitvision-phase0-visual-first-corrections.test.js` which verifies dual debug overlays, non-bbox geometry presence, geometry-faithful visual layer role, and panel-as-derived behavior, and this test passed. 
- Verified existing precompute regression `test/wrokitvision-precompute-phase1.test.js` which passed. 
- Verified compatibility regression `test/wrokitvision-phase15-corrections.test.js` which passed. 
- Performed syntax/load checks on modified engine modules and the bundled precompute adapter and confirmed they load without errors.

- The Adobe kit uses a **repo-level build and test orchestration** — the build concatenates \`AdobeSDKs/\` vendor files (VisitorAPI.js, AppMeasurement.js) with each package's source before running rollup, and tests run from the root using Jest with \`MODULE=client/server\` env vars. 💡 **What**: Switched `HashMap` to `BuildHasherDefault<IdentityHasher>` for `NodeId` keys in experimental pathfinding and graph traversal modules (`spectre`, `synapse`, `sybil`, `telepathy`).
🎯 **Why**: `NodeId` is a wrapper around a unique `u64`. Using the default cryptographic SipHash incurs unnecessary hashing overhead. In A* pathfinding and vector propagation simulations, maps are updated/looked up millions of times in a hot loop.
📊 **Impact**: Expected to drastically reduce map-lookup overhead and improve throughput during simulation iterations without fighting the borrow checker or introducing unsafe.
🔬 **Measurement**: Run global test suite (`cargo test`) to ensure functionality. Any graph benchmarks or deep depth searches in A* (`spectre.rs`) will highlight the improved overhead.

author: denniswebb
body:
## Summary

Terrakube creates **one GitHub webhook per workspace** (1:1 relationship). When a GitHub repository hosts 30-40 Terraform workspaces, it hits [GitHub's 20-webhook-per-repo limit](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/webhooks/repos). This PR introduces **shared repository-level webhooks** where a single GitHub hook per repository fans out to all workspaces using that repo.

## Problem

- Each workspace that enables webhooks creates its own GitHub webhook on the repository
- GitHub enforces a limit of 20 webhooks per repository
- Organizations with many Terraform workspaces backed by the same repo cannot enable webhooks for all of them
- This is a GitHub-specific limitation (GitLab/Bitbucket don't have this constraint)

## Solution

### New `vcs_webhook` table

One row per unique `(vcs_id, repository_url)` pair — one shared GitHub webhook per repo per VCS connection. A single VCS connection can have many repos, each with its own VcsWebhook.

| Column | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `id` | PK (UUID) |
| `vcs_id` | FK to VCS connection |
| `repository_url` | Normalized repo URL (lowercase, no `.git` suffix) |
| `remote_hook_id` | GitHub's webhook ID |
| `secret` | Random UUID used as HMAC secret for payload verification |

### Two coexisting callback paths

| Path | Mode | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `POST /webhook/v1/{webhookId}` | Legacy | Existing per-workspace webhooks, **completely unchanged** |
| `POST /webhook/v1/vcs/{vcsWebhookId}` | Shared | New fan-out endpoint for shared webhooks |

The **URL path alone** determines which mode handles the request. There is no ambiguity or runtime detection needed.

### How fan-out works

1. GitHub sends a push/PR/release event to `/webhook/v1/vcs/{vcsWebhookId}`
2. Load the `VcsWebhook` record, verify HMAC signature using its stored secret
3. Parse the payload once (branch, changed files, event type, commit)
4. Query all workspaces where `vcs = this VCS AND normalized(source) = this repo AND webhook IS NOT NULL`
5. For each workspace, check its `WebhookEvent` rules (branch regex, path regex, event type, priority)
6. Create a Job for each matching workspace (exceptions are caught per-workspace so one failure doesn't block others)
7. Workspaces with legacy per-workspace hooks (those with `remoteHookId` set) are skipped during fan-out — they receive events via their own `/webhook/v1/{webhookId}` path

### Key design decisions

**No FK from `webhook` to `vcs_webhook`:** The fan-out query uses the workspace's existing `vcs` and `source` fields to find matching workspaces. This means **zero changes to the existing `webhook` table schema**.

**Random secret per VcsWebhook:** Each shared webhook gets a `UUID.randomUUID()` as its HMAC secret, stored in the `secret` column. This is different from the legacy approach which uses `Base64(workspaceId)` as the secret. A random secret is more secure — if one repo's secret leaks, it doesn't compromise others. The legacy approach continues to work unchanged for existing webhooks.

**URL normalization:** Repository URLs are normalized (lowercase, strip `.git`, strip trailing `/`) for matching. This is done via a static `WebhookServiceBase.normalizeRepositoryUrl()` method used consistently across creation, deletion, and fan-out.

**GitHub only for now:** Only GitHub gets shared webhook support. GitLab and Bitbucket continue with per-workspace webhooks (GitLab doesn't have this limit; Bitbucket can be added later).

**Event type union:** When multiple workspaces share a webhook, the GitHub hook is configured with the **union** of all event types across those workspaces. For example, if workspace A subscribes to PUSH and workspace B subscribes to PUSH + PULL_REQUEST, the GitHub hook gets both event types. When a workspace is removed, the union is recalculated and the GitHub hook is PATCHed.

**Migration endpoint requires auth:** The new `/api/v1/webhook/{webhookId}/migrate` endpoint is placed under `/api/v1/` (not `/webhook/v1/`) so it goes through the standard authentication filter. The `/webhook/v1/**` paths are `permitAll()` since they receive unauthenticated payloads from VCS providers.

## Changes

### New files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `VcsWebhook.java` | JPA entity for `vcs_webhook` table |
| `VcsWebhookRepository.java` | Spring Data repository with `findByVcsAndRepositoryUrl` |
| `changelog-2.31.0-vcs-webhook.xml` | Liquibase migration (create table + unique constraint + FK) |

### Modified files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `WebhookService.java` | Core shared logic: creation, deletion cleanup, fan-out processing, migration |
| `WebhookServiceBase.java` | Added `normalizeRepositoryUrl()` and `handleWebhookWithSecret()` |
| `GitHubWebhookService.java` | Added `processSharedWebhook`, `createSharedWebhook`, `updateSharedWebhookEvents`, `deleteSharedWebhook` |
| `WebHookController.java` | Added shared inbound endpoint and authenticated migration endpoint |
| `WorkspaceRepository.java` | Added `findByVcsAndWebhookIsNotNull(Vcs)` query |
| `changelog.xml` | Registered new migration |
| `Webhook.tsx` | Alert banners for shared/legacy mode, "Migrate to shared" button |

### Unchanged

- `Webhook.java` — no entity changes
- `WebhookEvent.java` — no entity changes
- `webhook` table schema — no column additions or modifications
- Legacy `/webhook/v1/{webhookId}` processing — completely untouched

## Backward compatibility

- All existing per-workspace webhooks continue to work identically
- The legacy `processWebhook()` code path is not modified
- No database migration touches existing tables
- New webhooks on GitHub VCS connections automatically use shared mode
- A "Migrate to shared" button in the UI lets users opt-in for existing legacy webhooks

## Test plan

- [ ] Create webhook for workspace A on repo X → creates VcsWebhook + GitHub hook at `/v1/vcs/`
- [ ] Create webhook for workspace B on same repo → reuses VcsWebhook, no new GitHub API call
- [ ] Push to repo → `/webhook/v1/vcs/{id}` receives event, jobs created for both A and B based on their WebhookEvent rules
- [ ] Delete workspace A webhook → VcsWebhook persists, GitHub hook stays
- [ ] Delete workspace B webhook (last one) → VcsWebhook and GitHub hook both deleted
- [ ] Event union: workspace A has PUSH, workspace B has PUSH + PR → GitHub hook configured with both. Remove B → PATCHed to PUSH only
- [ ] Legacy webhooks: existing `/webhook/v1/{webhookId}` flow unchanged
- [ ] Migration: click "Migrate to shared" → old GitHub hook deleted, workspace uses shared VcsWebhook, WebhookEvent rules preserved
- [ ] Signature verification: shared endpoint uses VcsWebhook.secret, legacy uses Base64(workspace.id)

## Summary
Adjusted the vertical positioning of fixed trigger buttons in the NoticePanel and WeeklySyncPage components to use explicit pixel-based offsets instead of CSS transforms.

- **NoticePanel**: Changed the notice trigger button from `top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2` to `top-[calc(50%+1rem)]` to offset it slightly below the viewport center

author: drewthaler
body:
## Summary

Refactors the LLM extraction module (`llm_extract.py`) so the model provider and model ID are configurable rather than hardcoded to Anthropic/Haiku. This enables switching between Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash, and other models via environment variables alone.

### Changes

- **New `llm_providers.py`** — thin adapter layer with `call_llm()` dispatcher and per-provider adapters (Anthropic, Google GenAI). Each adapter handles auth, API calls, retries, and returns a unified `LLMResponse` dataclass with text + token counts.
- **Refactored `llm_extract.py`** — removed hardcoded Anthropic API calls (`_call_api`), now delegates to `call_llm()` from the provider layer. The extraction prompt, JSON parsing, chunking, and merge logic are shared across all providers.
- **Updated `worker.py`** — replaced `anthropic_client` constructor param with `llm_client`/`llm_provider`/`llm_model`. Uses `create_client()` factory for connection reuse. Reads `LLM_PROVIDER` and `LLM_MODEL` from env vars.
- **Added `google-genai>=1.0`** dependency to `pyproject.toml`.
- **23 new adapter tests** in `test_llm_providers.py` covering both providers, dispatch logic, env var resolution, client creation, retry behavior, and error handling.
- **Updated existing tests** to mock the provider-agnostic `call_llm` interface instead of Anthropic internals.

### Configuration

| Env Var | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` | Provider name: `anthropic` or `google` |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Per-provider default | Model ID (e.g. `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | — | Required for Anthropic provider |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | — | Required for Google provider |

Closes #449

body:
ManageOrders behavior regressed in two ways: it was running during AH pause despite expected gating, and cancellation was brittle enough that open orders were not being cancelled in many Bazaar UI variants. This PR restores pause-time gating and makes ManageOrders detect orders/actions from both name and lore metadata.

- **AH pause gating parity**
  - Reverted queue filter behavior so AH pause drops:
    - `BazaarBuyOrder`
    - `BazaarSellOrder`
    - `ManageOrders`
  - This restores the prior expectation that Bazaar management does not run while AH flip pause is active.

- **ManageOrders: robust order row detection**
  - Order slots are now recognized when either condition is true:
    - entry name matches known order patterns, or
    - lore parses to Bazaar identity (`Buy Order` / `Sell Offer` + item field).
  - This covers windows where display name is generic but lore carries the semantic role.

- **ManageOrders: robust action button detection**
  - Action selection still prefers name matching (`Collect` / `Claim` / `Cancel`).
  - Added lore fallbacks for localized/variant labels:
    - collect: `"click to collect"`, `"claim your"`
    - cancel: `"click to cancel"`, `"cancel order"`

- **Small internal cleanup**
  - Removed duplicate identity parsing in the order scan path.
  - Added helper-level coverage around lore phrase matching and lore-only order identification.

```rust
// During AH pause, block Bazaar placement + management commands.
fn should_drop_bazaar_command_during_ah_pause(
    command_type: &CommandType,

) -> bool {
    bazaar_flips_paused
        && matches!(
            command_type,
            CommandType::BazaarBuyOrder { .. }
                | CommandType::BazaarSellOrder { .. }
                | CommandType::ManageOrders { .. }

}

author: williballenthin
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `ApiModuleLoader` wrote raw PE file bytes into emulated memory, but PE sections have different file offsets vs virtual addresses. Shellcode walking the PEB `InInitializationOrderModuleList` to find kernel32 and parse its export directory would read garbage data because `.edata` was at its file offset rather than its virtual address.
- **Fix**: Use `pefile.get_memory_mapped_image()` so sections are placed at their correct virtual addresses, matching how Windows actually loads DLLs.
- **Bonus fix**: `Process.ldr_entries` was a shared class-level mutable list (classic Python gotcha) instead of per-instance, causing cross-test contamination. Moved to `__init__`.
- **Config fix**: Test config `test.json` now lists ntdll before kernel32, matching the default config order.

## Test plan

- [x] New `test_peb_shellcode.py` with two tests:
  - PEB walk shellcode resolves `WinExec` from kernel32 via `InInitializationOrderModuleList`
  - Same shellcode succeeds even when config has kernel32 before ntdll (verifying `_ordered_peb_modules()`)
- [x] All existing tests pass (47 passed, 1 skipped; 2 pre-existing failures from missing capa-testfiles)

author: ghostiee-11
body:
## Description

In mirror mode (when `self.tables` is empty), `DerivedSource.get()` assigns `transforms = self.transforms` which is a direct reference to the instance's list. The subsequent `transforms.append(FilterTransform(...))` permanently mutates `self.transforms`, causing:

- The transforms list to grow by one `FilterTransform` on every `.get()` call
- Stale filters from previous queries to accumulate and affect future results

The `tables` branch (line 1621) is safe because `+` creates a new list, but the mirror-mode `else` branch was missing a copy.

### Change

```diff
  else:
-     transforms = self.transforms
+     transforms = list(self.transforms)
```

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added regression test `test_derived_mirror_get_does_not_mutate_transforms` that calls `.get()` twice and verifies `self.transforms` length is unchanged.

```

## Description

Two fixes in `pipeline.py`:

**1. Loading state never reset on error (line 321-336)**

`_update_data` sets `self._update_widget.loading = True` at the start but only resets it at the end of the happy path. author: itsyoboieltr
body:
This PR prevents the plugin from running on files inside node_modules and preserves Bun's original loader for files that do go through the hook.

## Problem

I ran into a build failure because the plugin's `onLoad` hook was also matching dependency files from `node_modules`. As a result, dependencies were being read and passed through this plugin even though they are not part of the application's Lingui macro setup. In my case this showed up as a build error coming from a dependency that should not have been processed by this plugin in the first place. The root cause was not the dependency itself, but that the plugin was intercepting `node_modules` files too broadly.

## Change

This PR wraps babelRe with an additional check that excludes paths containing a `node_modules` segment, and uses that regex in `onLoad` instead of `babelRe`.

## Why this fix

The goal is to keep Lingui's existing source-extension matching, but limit it to project source files. Without this, the plugin can accidentally intercept third-party packages. With this change, the hook only runs for application files and leaves dependencies to Bun's normal resolution/loading behavior.

Collisions may go undetected since the contact sensor has a [history_length = 3](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/sru-navigation-sim/blob/03c42e1a59158f8301216a60d28e362873d51652/isaaclab_nav_task/navigation/navigation_env_cfg.py#L117) sim steps, while terminations are updated every 40 sim steps (`self.decimation`). This MR adjusts the contact sensor's history buffer to hold all contact forces that occur between high level policy updates.

body:
Fixes #169 

The README documented `SwiftResolved` as the detector ID for the Swift Package Manager detector, but the actual registered ID in [`SwiftResolvedComponentDetector.cs`](https://github.com/microsoft/component-detection/blob/main/src/Microsoft.ComponentDetection.Detectors/swiftpm/SwiftResolvedComponentDetector.cs) is `Swift`. Using `SwiftResolved=EnableIfDefaultOff` silently fails — the detector never activates.

## Changes

- **`README.md`**: Replace `SwiftResolved` with `Swift` in both the inline comment and the `detectorArgs` example

```yaml
# Before
# Default-off detectors: ConanLock, CondaLock, Dockerfile, Pip, SimplePip, Spdx22, SwiftResolved
detectorArgs: ...,SwiftResolved=EnableIfDefaultOff

# After
# Default-off detectors: ConanLock, CondaLock, Dockerfile, Pip, SimplePip, Spdx22, Swift
detectorArgs: ...,Swift=EnableIfDefaultOff
```

All other detector IDs in the example (`Poetry`, `UvLock`, `NpmLockfile3`, `Ivy`, `ConanLock`, `CondaLock`, `Dockerfile`, `Pip`, `SimplePip`, `Spdx22`) were verified against source and are correct.

author: catherinesue
body:
## Description

### Problem

The `check_release_versions.sh` script was missing `smg-grpc-servicer` from its `PYTHON_PACKAGES` registry, so version bumps for the gRPC servicer were never checked during releases.

Additionally, the existing `smg-grpc-proto` entry pointed at `__init__.py` which uses `importlib.metadata.version()` — the script's `sed` extraction was pulling out the package name (`smg-grpc-proto`) instead of the actual version number, so bump detection never worked for it either.

### Solution

- Add `smg-grpc-servicer` to `PYTHON_PACKAGES`
- Switch both entries to read version from `pyproject.toml` (the source of truth)
- Update `get_python_version`, `get_python_version_at_ref`, and `set_python_version` to handle `.toml` files alongside `__init__.py`

## Changes

- Point `smg-grpc-proto` version file at `pyproject.toml` instead of `__init__.py`
- Add `smg-grpc-servicer|grpc_servicer|grpc_servicer/pyproject.toml` entry
- Add `.toml` branch to version get/set helpers using the same `grep -m1 '^version'` pattern used for Cargo.toml

## Test Plan

- Verified `grep -m1 '^version' pyproject.toml | sed ...` extracts `0.4.2` for both packages
- Existing `__init__.py` codepath is preserved for any future packages that use hardcoded `__version__`

author: iloveitaly
body:
## Motivation

* Ruby source builds are slow. Users need to force precompiled binaries via `mise.toml` to speed up builds.
* `mise.lock` are not getting included in the `mise install` step which can cause shims to fail to run after the install step since they installed a different version that was present in the lockfile.

## Description

*   **Idiomatic version files**: Detect and use `.ruby-version`, `.node-version`, etc., during the `mise` installation step.
*   **User `mise` config**: Added support for `mise.toml` and `mise.local.toml`.
*   **Conflict Prevention**: Renamed the generated `mise` config to avoid naming collisions with user-provided files.
*   **Lockfile Support**: Added `mise.lock` support to the installation step for reproducible builds.
*   **Performance**: Cached the `mise` config file search.

This change _does_ meaningfully change the configuration present during mise install. This should fix issues for most users, but it could change things for some users and cause changes in their builds.

## Links

Resolves #232

author: copilot
body:
Consumer Lambda lacked retry logic for transient DynamoDB failures and had no timeout handling.

### Changes

- **Exponential backoff with jitter** — `store_item_with_retry()` retries transient DynamoDB errors (`ProvisionedThroughputExceededException`, `ThrottlingException`, `InternalServerError`, `ServiceUnavailable`, `RequestLimitExceeded`) up to `MAX_RETRIES` using full jitter: `random(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))`
- **Timeout handling** — Catches `ConnectTimeoutError` / `ReadTimeoutError`; boto3 configured with 5s connect and 10s read timeouts, SDK-level retries disabled (`max_attempts: 0`) since we manage retries
- **DLQ routing** — Failed messages reported via `batchItemFailures` response, SQS redrive policy handles DLQ routing after `maxReceiveCount`
- **Contextual logging** — All error paths log `messageId`, `requestId`, `error_type`, `error_code`, and attempt number
- Non-retryable `ClientError` codes (e.g. `ValidationException`) raise immediately without retry

```python
# Retry config is environment-configurable
MAX_RETRIES = int(os.environ.get("MAX_RETRIES", "3"))
BASE_DELAY_SECONDS = float(os.environ.get("BASE_DELAY_SECONDS", "0.1"))
MAX_DELAY_SECONDS = float(os.environ.get("MAX_DELAY_SECONDS", "2.0"))
```

37 unit tests covering backoff calculation, retry/timeout paths, non-retryable passthrough, and batch failure reporting.

author: julo0211
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: Potential Race Condition (TOCTOU) in Docker daemon.json creation, allowing a malicious symlink to overwrite arbitrary files if placed before `os.WriteFile`.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `os.Stat` and `os.WriteFile` with a secure, atomic `os.OpenFile` call using `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` flags to prevent symlink attacks, correctly falling back to a warning if the file already exists (`os.IsExist(err)`). Also added explicit `err := f.Close()` error checking to verify data flush safety.

author: ancyloce
body:
## Summary
- add Prometheus instrumentation to `email-worker` for send attempts, send latency, and queue backlog
- expose `GET /metrics` on a dedicated internal `email-worker` metrics listener and poll Redis backlog into a Prometheus gauge
- add version-controlled Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager config plus local Mailpit-backed email alert delivery
- add deployment wiring for `email-worker` and the monitoring stack, including worker image build/push and remote deploy updates
- document the monitoring stack, metrics, alerts, and local validation flow in `docs/monitoring.md`

## Monitoring / Alerting Notes
- `email_worker_send_attempts_total{result="success|failure"}` drives failure-rate calculations.
- `email_worker_send_latency_seconds{result="success|failure"}` is a histogram; Grafana computes average send latency from `sum/count`.
- `email_worker_queue_backlog{queue="<configured EMAIL_QUEUE_NAME>"}` is updated by polling Redis `LLEN` on `EMAIL_QUEUE_BACKLOG_POLL_SEC`.
- `email-worker` serves `/metrics` on the internal listener configured by `EMAIL_METRICS_ADDR` (default `:9090`), not on the public webhook listener.
- Prometheus scrapes `email-worker:9090/metrics`.
- Grafana provisions the `Email Worker Monitoring` dashboard from source-controlled JSON.
- Alert rules:
  - `EmailWorkerHighSendFailureRate`: failure rate > 5%
  - `EmailWorkerQueueBacklogHigh`: queue backlog > 1000 across exported queue series
- Alertmanager renders its config from environment variables at startup so email receiver settings stay configurable and out of git.
- Local alert delivery uses Mailpit as the SMTP sink and inbox viewer.

## Tests / Verification
### Passed
- `go test ./... -count=1` in `modules/common-go`
- `go test ./... -count=1` in `services/email-worker`
- `go test ./... -count=1` at repo root
- `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config`
- `docker compose --project-directory . --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml config`
- `docker run --rm --entrypoint promtool -v "$PWD/deploy/monitoring/prometheus/alerts:/rules:ro" prom/prometheus:v3.5.0 check rules /rules/email-worker.rules.yml`
- `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh -v "$PWD/deploy/monitoring/alertmanager:/config:ro" -e ALERT_EMAIL_TO=alerts@example.com -e ALERT_EMAIL_FROM=alerts@example.com -e ALERT_SMTP_SMARTHOST=mailpit:1025 -e ALERT_SMTP_AUTH_USERNAME= -e ALERT_SMTP_AUTH_PASSWORD="p@ss'word&with|chars\\andmore" -e ALERT_SMTP_REQUIRE_TLS=false prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1 -ec 'sh /config/render-alertmanager-config.sh /tmp/alertmanager.yml && amtool check-config /tmp/alertmanager.yml'`

### Runtime validation
- `/metrics` reachable from the internal `email-worker` metrics listener and exporting required metrics:
  - `email_worker_queue_backlog{queue="email:send"} 0`
  - `email_worker_send_attempts_total{result="failure"} 12`
  - `email_worker_send_latency_seconds_count{result="failure"} 12`
- Prometheus target healthy via `GET /api/v1/targets`:
  - `health: "up"` for `email-worker:9090`
- Grafana dashboard provisioned via API search:
  - dashboard title `Email Worker Monitoring`
  - dashboard uid `email-worker-overview`
- Alertmanager active alert validated via `GET /api/v2/alerts`:
  - `EmailWorkerHighSendFailureRate`
- Alert email delivery demonstrated in Mailpit via `GET /api/v1/messages`:
  - subject `[FIRING:1] EmailWorkerHighSendFailureRate email-worker (warning)`
  - from `alerts@anvilkit.local`
  - to `alerts@example.com`

### Not passing locally
- `go test ./... -count=1` in `services/auth-api` still has existing integration failures around handler/store deadlocks and verification flow state.
- `go test ./... -count=1` in `services/admin-api` still has existing handler integration failures around tenant/user FK setup.
- `golangci-lint` is not installed in this local environment, so I could not run the repo lint command here.

## Checklist Mapping
- define key metrics:
  - email send failure rate: implemented from `email_worker_send_attempts_total{result="failure"}` / total attempts
  - queue backlog length: implemented as `email_worker_queue_backlog`
  - average send latency: implemented as `email_worker_send_latency_seconds`
- use Prometheus + Grafana: added under `deploy/monitoring/` and wired into both compose files
- expose a `/metrics` endpoint from `email-worker`: added on the dedicated internal metrics listener configured by `EMAIL_METRICS_ADDR`
- configure alert rules:
  - failure rate > 5%: `EmailWorkerHighSendFailureRate`
  - queue backlog > 1000: `EmailWorkerQueueBacklogHigh`
- write `docs/monitoring.md`: added with setup, metrics, alerting, and local test instructions

## Acceptance Criteria Validation
- Grafana dashboard visualizes email-related metrics:
  - provisioned dashboard `Email Worker Monitoring` includes queue backlog, failure rate, average latency, and send throughput panels
  - verified through Grafana API search after startup
- alert notifications are sent when alerts trigger (Slack or Email):
  - Alertmanager email receiver configured
  - verified by forcing worker send failures, observing `EmailWorkerHighSendFailureRate` in Alertmanager, and receiving the firing email in Mailpit

## Assumptions
- Prometheus + Grafana was chosen because the repository did not already standardize on another monitoring platform.
- Email notifications were used instead of Slack because they are easier to demonstrate locally without external secrets and fit the issue scope.
- Production deploy wiring was extended to include `email-worker` and the monitoring stack so the checked-in monitoring config is deployable, not dev-only.

Fixes #89

body:
Discusion: https://github.com/iNavFlight/inav/issues/11065#issuecomment-4025281454

The PR is adding basic support for softRF for Nano-Edition, see https://github.com/lyusupov/SoftRF/wiki/Nano-Edition 

SoftRF supports FLARM and FANET protocols which are widely used by small planes in low altitudes. Good benefit for UAV to know about them. 

**Required by softRf**
```
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_HEARTBEAT 
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_SYSTEM_TIME 
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_GPS_RAW_INT
```

**Message which are not implemented** 
```
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_SYS_STATUS
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_VFR_HUD
MAVLINK_MSG_ID_ATTITUDE
```

The PR just add one new message MAVLINK_MSG_ID_SYSTEM_TIME. MAVLINK_MSG_ID_HEARTBEAT  has been refactored, now MAVLINK_MSG_ID_HEARTBEAT  is sent always, not only witgh HUD message as it was before. 

ADSB.md is updated as well.

- [x]  comminication softRF (FLARM ) <-> softRf (FLARM ) tested by SAMUD
- [x]  comminication softRF (ADSB-L) <-> softRf (ADSB-L) tested by SAMUD
- [x]  comminication softRF (FLARM ) <-> original FLARM defice on big plane  tested by SAMUD

author: charles-forsyth
body:
## Summary
This release transforms Radar into a proactive intelligence harvester by adding autonomous news wire ingestion.

### Key Features:
- **RSS Ingest Agent:** Added `RSSIngestAgent` to fetch and parse full-text content from critical technical feeds (RTL-SDR, Hackaday, HPCwire, CISA).
- **Proactive Ingestion:** Integrated news wire harvesting directly into the `radar sync --daily` command. Radar now "reads" the latest global tech developments twice a day automatically.
- **Direct Database Persistence:** Implemented `save_ingest_to_db` to streamline the transfer of scraped news into the Knowledge Graph.
- **Sophisticated Synthesis:** Enhanced the briefing agent to correlate these new global news signals with local tactical data.

### Engineering Updates:
- Optimized `RSSIngestAgent` with concurrent fetching and robust error handling.
- Passed strict Skywalker Local Gauntlet (ruff, mypy, pytest).
- Version bumped to v0.6.0.

body:
### Motivation

- Replace an overly difficult math captcha on the admin login with a simple, user-friendly challenge to reduce support friction.  
- Improve the membership application UX by supporting AJAX submission with inline success/error feedback.  
- Add an admin-side workflow to mark applications as "called" and to delete applications, and persist that state in the database.

### Description

- Replace the complex square-root/log captcha in `admin/login.php` with a simple addition captcha produced by `set_captcha()` that picks two integers in `1..20` and stores the expected sum.  
- Add an `is_called TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to the `membership_applications` schema in `inc/bootstrap.php` and include an `ALTER TABLE` fallback for existing installs.  
- Update `admin/memberships/index.php` to fetch `is_called`, style called applications with an `.is-called` class (blur/opacity), and add POST handlers and inline forms (with CSRF) to toggle `is_called` and to delete applications, with a redirect back to the list after actions.  
- Update the public `membership.php` form to support AJAX submissions by detecting `X-Requested-With`, returning JSON on success (`ok:true` with a localized `SUCCESS_TEXT`) or failure, keep a non-AJAX fallback redirect to `?submitted=1`, and add client-side JS to submit the form via `fetch`, show inline success/error messages, and reset the form on success.

### Testing

- Performed PHP syntax checks with `php -l` on the modified files and they passed.  
- No automated unit tests were added for this change set.

## Summary

- Problem: the docs still blur file-based hooks, plugin lifecycle hooks, and plugin-managed legacy hook registration into one generic “hooks” concept.
- Why it matters: that ambiguity keeps driving middleware/security proposals toward the wrong surface and makes `api.registerHook(...)` look like the default API instead of the compatibility bridge.
- What changed: `docs/automation/hooks.md` now defines the operator-automation boundary for HOOK-style hooks, and `docs/tools/plugin.md` now makes `api.on(...)` the preferred runtime lifecycle/middleware surface while documenting `api.registerHook(...)` as the legacy internal-hook bridge.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no runtime hook behavior changed in this PR, and OTEL/diagnostic-event guidance stays out of scope for a follow-up docs pass.

- Docs now explicitly tell users when to choose HOOK.md hooks vs typed plugin hooks.

author: zfcmoe
body:
The project does currently not work on some Linux distros, such as CentOS Stream, due to the shared libraries requiring a recent glibc version. Also more obscure operating systems, such as FreeBSD are also not supported. This has already been pointed out by [issue #30 30](https://github.com/MinnDevelopment/jdave/issues/30)

This is a fairly simple fix, where one can depend only on club.mincced:jdave-api, and provide the library file separately by specifying a path as `LIBDAVE_PATH=/opt/libdave.so java -jar bot.jar`. 

This also avoids reading a shared library from `/tmp/`, which has some security implications I'm not a fan of.

author: emernic
body:
## Summary
Three targeted changes to shorten the late-game "hopeless phase" without adding new systems:

- **Collapsed regions earn zero income** — society has broken down, no economic contribution
- **2 personnel lost per collapse** — staff in the fallen region are gone
- **Broader mercy rule** — when 4+ regions collapsed AND no research active, defeat triggers in 2 days (vs 5 days for classic zero-agency). Catches "has money but nothing useful to do"

## Design rationale
The issue (#740) proposed 4 new systems (triage, emergency research, last-resort policies, cascading consequences). Instead of adding complexity, these changes accelerate the existing defeat path: collapse → income loss → broke → mercy rule. The broader mercy trigger catches the edge case where income from large surviving regions (Asia = 60% of global income) keeps the player solvent even with 4+ collapses.

The remaining acceptance criteria (new spending options, guaranteed <5 day hopeless phase) may need follow-up work if playtesting shows the phase still drags.

Closes #740

### Motivation
- Short samples that loop repeatedly could stop streaming while DSP/UI continue because loop/seek transitions desynchronized streamer consumption. 
- Investigation pointed to loop handling and seek logic in the voice manager as the likely root cause. 

### Description
- Keep the loop restart target stable by always using `loop_start_frame` for the next loop instead of forcing the start to `0` (remove logic that overwrote the configured loop start).
- Add `seek_retry_count` to `voice_t` to track repeated failed seek attempts while `seek_pending` remains set.
- Initialize/reset `seek_retry_count` in `voice_clear()` and on trigger, clear it when a seek succeeds, and increment it when a seek attempt fails and remains pending.
- Changes touch `voice_manager.h` (add `seek_retry_count`) and `voice_manager.c` (loop restart logic and seek retry bookkeeping). These changes preserve the streamer/voice alignment and make failed seeks observable.

### Testing
- Performed automated static inspections (`rg`/code searches) for the key symbols and call sites which succeeded and confirmed updated code paths reference the new field.
- Verified the source diffs and relevant line-level context to ensure the loop restart and seek commit logic were modified as intended, with all inspection commands returning success.

author: copilot
body:
`subscribe()` vazava background tasks sem retornar handle; o driver Redis era stub in-process; `WorkflowEngine` não tinha integração com persistência ou EventBus; tabelas de persistência não existiam.

## `Cargo.toml`
- Features opcionais: `local-bus` (default), `redis-bus`, `local-workflows`, `redis-workflows`, `distributed`
- Dependência `redis = "0.24"` gated por `dep:redis` — `cargo build` sem flags não puxa Redis

## `src/events.rs`
- **`subscribe()`** agora retorna `anyhow::Result<SubscriptionHandle>` (era `()`) — compatível com código existente que descarta o resultado, pois drop de `JoinHandle` não cancela a task
- **Redis backend real** sob `#[cfg(feature = "redis-bus")]`: campos `redis_publisher`/`redis_channel` na struct, `publish()` usa `PUBLISH`, `subscribe_with_id()` usa `AsyncPubSub`; `init_redis()` inicializa o `ConnectionManager`
- **`AuditInterceptor`** persiste cada evento em `event_audit` com `match` explícito por variante (sem `format!("{:?}")` frágil)
- 6 testes unitários cobrindo: handle/cancel, grouping release/clear, interceptor

```rust
// Antes — handle descartado, sem cancelamento possível
bus.subscribe(handler).await?; // anyhow::Result<()>

// Agora
let handle = bus.subscribe(handler).await?; // anyhow::Result<SubscriptionHandle>
// ... depois:
handle.cancel(); // aborta a task de recepção
```

## `src/sagas.rs`
- `WorkflowEngine::execute_persistent()` — delega para `Saga::run_persistent()` por nome com idempotência via `transaction_id`
- `WorkflowEngine::execute_persistent_with_events()` — idem + publica `on_complete`/`on_failure` no `EventBus` após desfecho

## `migrations/20260309000001_workflow_persistence.sql`
- Types: `workflow_state`, `step_state` (idempotentes com `DO $$ BEGIN…EXCEPTION`)
- Tabelas: `workflow_executions` (estado global + idempotência), `workflow_steps` (estado por passo), `event_audit` (log do `AuditInterceptor`)

## Docs
- `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`: nova seção "Fase 6 — EventBus & Sagas" com tabelas de mudanças; contagem de testes 323 → 329; Fases 3 e 5 de prioridades atualizadas
- `PROMPTS_SEQUENCIAIS.md`: bloco ✅ CONCLUÍDO no topo
- `README.md`: tabelas de comparação e features atualizadas

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Contexto

Este é um port do MedusaJS para Rust. O PR #13 implementou a base funcional do EventBus e Sagas, mas gaps críticos precisam ser resolvidos.

## Estado Atual Analisado

### `src/events.rs` — Gaps identificados:
1. **Redis/SQS são stubs** — `with_driver(BusDriver::Redis)` apenas loga e usa in-process broadcast igual ao Local
2. **`subscribe()` não retorna handle** — retorna `anyhow::Result<()>`, impossibilitando cancelamento (memory leak)
3. Resto (grouping, interceptors, `subscribe_with_id`) já está implementado ✅

### `src/sagas.rs` — Gaps identificados:
1. **`SagaStorage` trait e `PostgresSagaStorage`** já estão implementados ✅
2. **`run_persistent()`** já está implementado ✅
3. **`WorkflowEngine` sem integração com EventBus** — não tem `execute_persistent()` e não dispara eventos

### `Cargo.toml` — Gaps:
- Sem feature flags para Redis (dependência `redis` não existe)

### `migrations/` — Gaps:
- `migrations/20260309000001_workflow_persistence.sql` não existe ainda

---

## Tarefas a Implementar

### PARTE 1: Cargo.toml — Adicionar features Redis opcionais

Adicionar ao `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[features]
default = ["local-bus", "local-workflows"]
manual_plugin = []

# Event Bus modes
local-bus = []
redis-bus = ["dep:redis"]

# Workflow modes  
local-workflows = []
redis-workflows = ["dep:redis"]

# Full distributed mode
distributed = ["redis-bus", "redis-workflows"]

[dependencies]
# ... existing deps ...
# Opcional - só com features redis
redis = { version = "0.24", features = ["aio", "tokio-comp", "connection-manager", "streams"], optional = true }
```

### PARTE 2: `src/events.rs` — Corrigir Redis driver + `subscribe()` API

**Problema 1**: `subscribe()` retorna `anyhow::Result<()>` — precisa retornar `anyhow::Result<SubscriptionHandle>`.

Alterar a assinatura de:
```rust
pub async fn subscribe<H>(&self, handler: H) -> anyhow::Result<()>
where H: EventHandler + Send + 'static,
{
    let _ = self.subscribe_with_id(handler, None).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
Para:
```rust
pub async fn subscribe<H>(&self, handler: H) -> anyhow::Result<SubscriptionHandle>
where H: EventHandler + Send + 'static,
{
    self.subscribe_with_id(handler, None).await
}
```

**Problema 2**: Redis driver é stub. Implementar backend real com `#[cfg(feature = "redis-bus")]`:

Refatorar `src/events.rs` para que `with_driver(BusDriver::Redis)` realmente use Redis pub/sub quando compilado com `--features redis-bus`. Criar novo módulo `src/events/` com:
- `src/events/mod.rs` — re-exporta tudo, mantém `EventBus`, `Event`, `EventHandler`, etc.  
- `src/events/redis_backend.rs` — implementação Redis gated por `#[cfg(feature = "redis-bus")]`

OU (mais simples, sem quebrar imports existentes): manter `src/events.rs` mas adicionar o backend Redis dentro do próprio arquivo com `#[cfg(feature = "redis-bus")]`.

**Implementação do Redis backend dentro de `src/events.rs`**:

```rust
// Adicionar ao EventBus::with_driver quando feature redis-bus está ativa:
// A struct EventBus precisa de um campo para o sender Redis opcional

// Adicionar struct e impl apenas com feature flag:
#[cfg(feature = "redis-bus")]
mod redis_impl {
    use super::*;
    use redis::aio::ConnectionManager;
    
    pub struct RedisPublisher {
        pub conn_manager: ConnectionManager,
        pub channel: String,
    }
    
    impl RedisPublisher {
        pub async fn new(redis_url: &str, channel: String) -> anyhow::Result<Self> {
            let client = redis::Client::open(redis_url)?;
            let conn_manager = ConnectionManager::new(client).await?;
            Ok(Self { conn_manager, channel })
        }
        
        pub async fn publish(&self, event: &super::Event) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
            let json = serde_json::to_string(event)?;
            let mut conn = self.conn_manager.clone();
            redis::cmd("PUBLISH")
                .arg(&self.channel)
                .arg(json)
                .query_async(&mut conn)
                .await?;
            tracing::debug!(channel = %self.channel, "Published event to Redis");
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}
```

**Abordagem alternativa mais limpa** — modificar `EventBus` para ter um campo `redis_publisher` opcional:

```rust
pub struct EventBus {
